Mizoram PSC Final Result 2026 for MAS and MHS Posts - Complete Details

The Mizoram Public Service Commission (MPSC) has officially released the final result for the Jr. Grade of Mizoram Agriculture Service (MAS) and Jr. Grade of Mizoram Horticulture Service (MHS) recruitment. Candidates recommended for appointment have been notified in order of merit through Notification No. A.12031/8/2026-MPSC(PE), dated 16th June 2026. This final result follows the Agriculture & Allied Services (Combined Technical) Examination, 2025, and the subsequent Personal Interview round, marking the conclusive stage of this recruitment cycle.

This result is significant for candidates who applied under Advertisement No. 2 of 2025-26 for posts under the Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare Department and the Horticulture Department, Government of Mizoram. Below is a complete, fact-based breakdown of the notification, the selection process, and the merit list released so far.

Click Here: Mizoram PSC Final Result 2026

What Is the Mizoram PSC MAS & MHS Final Result 2026?

This section explains the core purpose of the notification and which posts and departments it covers, so candidates can quickly confirm whether the result applies to them.

The Mizoram PSC has notified candidates recommended for appointment to two specific posts:

  • Jr. Grade of Mizoram Agriculture Service (MAS) - under the Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare Department
  • Jr. Grade of Mizoram Horticulture Service (MHS) - under the Horticulture Department

These appointments are made on the basis of the Agriculture & Allied Services (Combined Technical) Examination, 2025, conducted in line with Advertisement No. 2 of 2025-26, dated 20.06.2025. The recommended candidates are listed strictly in order of merit, based on their combined performance in the written examination and personal interview.

Key Details of the Mizoram PSC Final Result 2026

This section summarizes the essential facts of the notification in a single, scannable format, ideal for a quick overview of the recruitment timeline.

Particulars Details
Notification No. A.12031/8/2026-MPSC(PE)
Issuing Authority Mizoram Public Service Commission (MPSC)
Date of Notification 16th June 2026
Posts Covered Jr. Grade MAS, Jr. Grade MHS
Departments Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare Dept.; Horticulture Dept.
Advertisement Reference Advertisement No. 2 of 2025-26, dated 20.06.2025
Examination Name Agriculture & Allied Services (Combined Technical) Examination, 2025
Written Exam Dates 25th - 27th November 2025
Personal Interview Dates 8th - 16th June 2026
Result Basis Order of merit (Written + Interview marks)

Selection Process for MAS & MHS Recruitment 2025-26

This section explains how candidates were shortlisted and ranked, helping applicants understand the basis on which the final merit list was prepared.

The recruitment process for both MAS and MHS posts followed a structured two-stage evaluation:

  1. Written Examination - The Agriculture & Allied Services (Combined Technical) Examination, 2025 was conducted over three days, from 25th to 27th November 2025.
  2. Personal Interview - Shortlisted candidates from the written exam were called for a Personal Interview, held over an extended window from 8th to 16th June 2026.

The final merit position of each candidate was determined by the total marks secured in both the written examination and personal interview combined, as reflected in the "Total Marks" column of the official result.

How to Check the Mizoram PSC Final Result 2026

This section provides a simple step-by-step guide for candidates who want to verify their name or roll number in the official notification.

Candidates can verify their selection status by following these steps:

  • Visit the official MPSC website: mpsc.mizoram.gov.in
  • Navigate to the "Results" section on the homepage
  • Look for the notification titled "Final Result of Agri & Allied (MAS & MHS), 2025"
  • Open the PDF and locate your roll number under the relevant post (MAS or MHS)
  • Download or save the notification for future reference, including for joining formalities

What Happens After the Final Result Is Declared?

This section outlines the typical next steps for candidates whose names appear in the merit list, based on standard MPSC recruitment procedure.

Once a final result is declared in order of merit, recommended candidates are generally required to:

  • Await formal appointment orders or joining instructions from the respective department (Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare Department or Horticulture Department)
  • Complete document verification as specified by the appointing authority
  • Report for duty within the timeline communicated in the appointment letter

Candidates should rely only on official communication from MPSC or the concerned department for further procedural updates, as specific post-result instructions were not detailed within the scope of this notification excerpt.

The Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) has released the result of the Jharkhand Trained Madhyamik Acharya Combined Competitive Examination (JTMACCE) 2025 on 16 June 2026. This result, issued under Advertisement No. 02/2025, lists the roll numbers of candidates declared successful against vacant posts of Madhyamik Acharya (Secondary Teacher) across multiple subject categories, including Santhali, Ho, Kurmali, Kudukh, Mundari, Odia, Panchpargania, Bangla, Khortha, Nagpuri, and Urdu. How to Check Airforce Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen Intake 01/2027 Result

Checking the result is a simple online process that requires login credentials issued at the time of application. This section explains each step needed to view and download your result.

To check the Airforce Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen Intake 01/2027 Result, follow these steps:

  1. Visit the official website of the Indian Air Force.
  2. On the homepage, locate and open the "Agniveer / Airmen Recruitment" section.
  3. Click on the link titled "Airmen Group Y (Medical Assistant) Intake 01/2027 Result."
  4. You will be redirected to the login page.
  5. Enter your login details, including your Email ID / Registration Number and Password.
  6. Click on the "Login / Submit" button.
  7. Your result will be displayed on the screen.
  8. Download the result PDF and take a printout for future reference.

Application Fee Details

Knowing the correct application fee helps candidates verify their payment status against official requirements. The fee structure for this recruitment was category-based, as shown below.

Category Application Fee
General / OBC / EWS ₹550 + 18% GST
SC / ST ₹550 + 18% GST

Payment for the online application could be made through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, IMPS, or Cash Card / Mobile Wallet.

Eligibility Criteria for Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen

Eligibility for this post depends on educational qualification and falls into two distinct pathways. This section outlines the academic and age requirements for each.

Educational Qualification

Trade Pathway Eligibility Criteria
Medical Assistant Trade Pass in 10+2 / Intermediate (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English, securing minimum 50% aggregate marks and 50% in English; OR a two-year vocational course in the same non-vocational subjects with identical minimum marks from a recognized board.
Medical Assistant Trade (Diploma / B.Sc in Pharmacy) Pass in 10+2 / Intermediate with Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English (minimum 50% aggregate and 50% in English) AND a Diploma or B.Sc in Pharmacy with minimum 50% aggregate marks, along with valid registration from the State Pharmacy Council or the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI).

Age Limit

Age eligibility differs based on the qualification pathway and marital status:

  • Medical Assistant Trade (10+2 pathway): Unmarried candidates born between 01 January 2006 and 01 January 2010 (both dates inclusive).
  • Medical Assistant Trade (Diploma / B.Sc in Pharmacy pathway):
    1. Unmarried candidates born between 01 January 2003 and 01 January 2008 (both dates inclusive).
    2. Married candidates born between 01 January 2003 and 01 January 2006 (both dates inclusive).
  • Upper Age Limit: 21 years (additional age relaxation may apply as per the official notification).

Candidates should refer to the detailed notification for specific age relaxation rules applicable to certain categories.

Physical Fitness Test (PFT) and Medical Standards

Beyond academics, candidates must meet defined physical and medical benchmarks to qualify for this trade. This section covers the running test, height, hearing, dental, and visual standards required.

Parameter Standard
Physical Fitness Test (up to 21 years) 1.6 km run within 7 minutes
Physical Fitness Test (above 21 years, Diploma/B.Sc Pharmacy holders) 1.6 km run within 7 minutes 30 seconds
Minimum Height 152.5 cm
Chest Expansion Well-proportioned and well-developed, minimum expansion of 5 cm
Hearing Must be able to hear a forced whisper from 6 meters in each ear separately
Weight Proportionate to height and age, as per IAF standards
Dental Health Healthy gums, good set of teeth, minimum 14 dental points
Visual Standards 6/36 in each eye, correctable to 6/9; refractive error not exceeding +3.50D including astigmatism

Selection Process for Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen

Candidates often want to know the complete selection journey after the written exam. This section breaks down each stage of the IAF's selection process for this trade.

The mode of selection for the Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen Intake 01/2027 includes the following stages:

  • Proficiency Test
  • English Written Test
  • Physical Fitness Test (Phase I & II)
  • Adaptability Test - II
  • Medical Examination/Appointments

Candidates must clear each stage sequentially to be considered for final selection.

How to Download PSSSB Result 2026 PDF

Candidates can check and download the SSSB Punjab Result 2026 PDF for any of the above posts by following these simple steps. The result is published in PDF format and contains roll numbers of all qualified candidates along with the Common Merit List (CML).

  5. Press Ctrl+F (Windows) or Cmd+F (Mac) to open the search bar and type your Roll Number.
  6. If your roll number appears, you are qualified / selected.
  7. Download and save the PDF for future reference and document verification.

What is a Result - cum-CML (Common Merit List)?

A Result-cum-CML (Common Merit List) published by SSSB Punjab is a combined document that serves two purposes. It announces the result of the written examination and also presents a merit list of all qualifying candidates ranked by their marks. This merit list is used for subsequent selection stages such as counselling, document verification, or appointment.

  • Result: Declares which candidates have passed the written examination.
  • CML (Common Merit List): Ranks all qualifying candidates across categories based on marks obtained.
  • How it is used: Candidates on the CML are called for document verification / counselling in merit order up to the number of available vacancies.
  • Tie-breaking rule: In case of equal marks, the older candidate is generally given preference. If age is also equal, marks in the qualifying examination are considered.

What to Do After Checking the PSSSB Result 2026

  • Do not submit any fee or documents to unauthorized sources. All communications will be through the official PSSSB website only.
  • Regularly check sssb.punjab.gov.in for notices related to your post and advertisement number.

For Candidates Not in the Result List

  • Check your roll number carefully in the correct PDF for your post and advertisement number.
  • If you believe there is a discrepancy, contact SSSB Punjab through official channels.
  • Stay updated for any supplementary list or provisional list that may be released subsequently.

How to Check and Download the Agniveer Vayu Intake 01/2027 Result

Candidates often want to know the exact login process to access their scorecard without errors. The steps below outline how to retrieve the result using the credentials created at the time of application.

  1. Visit the official Agniveer Vayu recruitment portal at agnipathvayu.cdac.in or indianairforce.nic.in.

Stream Duration Subjects Covered

Other Than Science Stream 45 minutes English, Reasoning, General Awareness (RAGA)

The exam was conducted in objective (multiple-choice) format only. Reports indicate the Agniveer Vayu Intake 01/2027 recruitment drive received over 36 lakh applications, reflecting the scale of competition for this intake.

Indian Airforce Agniveer Vayu Merit List 2027

The merit list is a separate but related document that candidates frequently confuse with the result. This section clarifies how it is prepared and why it matters for progressing to the next stage.

The merit list contains the roll numbers and names of candidates who have secured the qualifying marks in the Phase-I written exam and have been shortlisted for Phase-II. It is prepared based on:

  • Marks scored in the Phase-I online examination
  • Category-wise reservation norms
  • Total number of vacancies notified
  • Overall competition level for the intake

Only candidates whose names or roll numbers appear in the merit list will be called for Phase-II testing.

Selection Process After the Agniveer Vayu Result

Once the result is declared, candidates often want clarity on what comes next in the recruitment journey. The Indian Air Force selection process for Agniveer Vayu runs across three structured phases.

Phase-I: Online Written Examination

This stage has already been completed and assessed, and the result declared on 16 June 2026 reflects performance in this phase.

Phase-II: Physical Fitness Test (PFT) and Adaptability Tests

Shortlisted candidates undergo physical fitness checks and adaptability assessments. The expected fitness benchmarks include:

  • Running: 1.6 km within the prescribed time limit (separate timing for male and female candidates)
  • 10 Push-ups within 1 minute (male candidates)
  • 10 Sit-ups within 1 minute for males, 1 minute 30 seconds for females
  • 20 Squats within 1 minute for males; 15 squats within 1 minute for females
  • Adaptability Test-I and Test-II, which evaluate mental agility, decision-making, and suitability for service conditions

Phase-III: Document Verification and Medical Examination

Candidates who clear Phase-II proceed to detailed document verification followed by a medical examination as per IAF medical standards, which includes height, weight, chest measurement, vision, and overall physical fitness checks.

Only candidates who successfully clear all three phases are considered for final selection as Agniveer Vayu.

Eligibility Criteria for Agniveer Vayu Intake 01/2027

This section is useful for candidates planning to apply to future intakes or verifying whether their original application met the laid-down eligibility norms.

Educational Qualification

  • Passed 10+2 (Intermediate) with Mathematics, Physics, and English, securing a minimum of 50% aggregate marks and 50% marks in English, OR

  • A 2-year vocational course with Physics and Mathematics as non-vocational subjects from a recognized board, with 50% aggregate and 50% marks in English

Other Than Science Stream:

  • Passed 10+2 (Intermediate) with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks and 50% marks in English, OR
  • A 2-year vocational course with a minimum of 50% aggregate and 50% marks in English

Age Limit

Candidates were required to be between 17.5 and 22 years of age, born between 01 January 2006 and 01 July 2009 (both dates inclusive), as per IAF age relaxation rules applicable to this intake.

Beyond academic eligibility, candidates must also meet specific physical standards. This table summarizes the height, chest, and fitness benchmarks set by the Indian Air Force.

How to Check UPSC Prelims Result 2026 Name Wise Online

The UPSC Civil Services Main Examination 2026 is scheduled for 21st August 2026. This leaves limited time, so candidates should immediately begin focused preparation for the nine descriptive papers in the Mains exam.

Candidates must regularly check upsc.gov.in for notifications related to the DAF, Mains admit card, exam centres, and schedule.

Keep all original documents ready, including educational certificates, category certificates (if applicable), identity proof, and the Prelims admit card.

  • Qualified candidates must fill out their cadre preferences for the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 from 19 June to 28 June 2026 with a fee of ₹200, unless they are female, PwBD, SC, or ST candidates. 

How to Check UPSC Prelims Result 2026 Online - Step-by-Step

Candidates should follow the official process to verify their qualifying status from the UPSC result PDF. Since the UPSC website experiences extremely heavy traffic immediately after result announcements, using the direct PDF link above is the fastest approach.

  1. Visit the Official UPSC Website - Open upsc.gov.in on your browser.
  2. Go to the "What's New" Section - Scroll down on the homepage to find the latest notifications panel.
  3. Click on the Result Link - Look for "Result: Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination, 2026" and click it.
  4. Download the PDF - A new tab will open with a link to the official roll number list. Download the PDF to your device.
  5. Search Your Roll Number or Name - Open the PDF and press Ctrl + F (PC) or use the in-app search (mobile). Type your 7-digit roll number or name to check if you have qualified.

UPSC CSE Prelims Result 2026 - Name-wise vs Roll Number-wise PDF

UPSC typically releases two separate PDFs - one arranged by roll number and one arranged alphabetically by name. Both are accessible via the official website.

How to Check UPSC Prelims Result 2026 Name-wise

The name-wise PDF lists all qualified candidates in alphabetical order. Candidates can open the PDF and use Ctrl + F to search their full name. In case of a common name, cross-check the corresponding roll number to confirm your entry.

How to Check UPSC Prelims Result 2026 Roll Number-wise

The roll number-wise PDF is the primary official result document released first. Candidates should:

  • Open the downloaded PDF.
  • Press Ctrl + F and enter their unique 7-digit UPSC roll number.
  • If the roll number appears in the list, the candidate has qualified for UPSC Mains 2026.

Details Mentioned in the UPSC CSE Prelims Result 2026 PDF

The official result PDF released by UPSC at upsc.gov.in contains the following information:

  • Name of the Examination (Civil Services Preliminary Examination, 2026)
  • Roll numbers of all candidates who have qualified
  • Important instructions for qualified candidates regarding next steps
  • Information regarding DAF-I (Detailed Application Form) for Mains
  • Official notice from the Commission
  • Schedule details for the Mains Examination

What to Do After UPSC CSE Prelims Result 2026 - Next Steps for Qualified Candidates

Qualifying the Prelims is just the first step. Candidates who find their name or roll number in the result PDF must immediately take the following actions within the prescribed deadlines to remain eligible for the Mains stage.

Step 1 - Fill DAF-I (Detailed Application Form for Mains)

The application window for DAF-I will remain open from 19 June to 28 June 2026 on the official portal upsconline.nic.in. Candidates must log in and fill in or reconfirm personal information, educational details, examination preferences, and cadre preferences. 

Step 2 - Pay the Mains Application Fee

Candidates who qualify for the Civil Services (Mains) Examination 2026 are required to pay an application fee of ₹200. Female candidates, SC, ST, and PwBD applicants are fully exempted from this fee payment. 

Step 3 - Prepare for UPSC CSE Mains 2026

The UPSC Mains Exam 2026 is scheduled to begin on 21 August 2026 and will continue for five days. Qualified candidates should immediately shift their focus entirely to Mains preparation, covering essay, general studies (GS I-IV), and optional subject papers. 

UPSC Civil Services Exam - Selection Process Overview

Understanding the three-stage selection process helps qualified Prelims candidates plan their next steps effectively.

The Civil Services Examination is conducted in three stages:

Stage Exam Type Marks Nature
Prelims (Paper I - GS) Objective MCQ 200 Screening (for merit)
Prelims (Paper II - CSAT) Objective MCQ 200 Qualifying (min. 33%)
Mains (9 Papers) Descriptive 1,750 + 600 (optional) Merit-based
Personality Test (Interview) Oral 275 Merit-based

Important points to remember:

  • The Prelims examination acts purely as a screening stage. Marks from this exam do not contribute to the final merit list. 
  • CSAT (Paper II) is qualifying in nature. Candidates need to score at least 33% (66.66 marks out of 200) for their General Studies Paper I to be evaluated
  • The Mains examination consists of nine papers, of which two language papers are qualifying in nature.

UPSC CSE Prelims Cut-Off 2026 - When Will It Be Released?

One of the most searched queries after result declaration is about the official UPSC Prelims 2026 cut-off marks. Here is what candidates need to know.

As mentioned in the result PDF, the marks, cut-off marks, and final answer keys for the CS (P) Examination 2026 will be uploaded on the Commission's website only after the completion of the entire Civil Services Examination 2026 and Indian Forest Service Examination 2026, i.e., after the final results are declared.

CIDCO (City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra) has officially declared the result for the post of Assistant Engineer (Civil), based on the online examination conducted on 21 July 2025. The result includes the provisional merit list, category-wise select list, and waiting list for candidates who applied against the recruitment advertisement dated 18 January 2024. Candidates can check their roll number, marks obtained, category, and selection status directly from the official CIDCO result PDF.

This section gives a quick summary of the key details related to the CIDCO Assistant Engineer (Civil) recruitment result, including the exam date, post name, and the nature of the released lists.

Particulars Details
Organisation CIDCO (City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited)

Result Status Merit List, Select List & Waiting List Declared

Result Nature Provisional, subject to document verification

Download CIDCO Assistant Engineer Result 2026

What Does the CIDCO AE (Civil) Result PDF Contain?

The official result document is divided into multiple sections so that candidates can easily check their selection status, category-wise ranking, and overall marks. Here is what each section covers.

1. Merit List

The merit list shows candidates arranged in descending order of total marks obtained out of 210 (online exam marks plus applicable SAP/additional marks). Against each candidate's name, the list mentions their roll number, applied category, total marks, and a remarks column indicating eligibility status.

For example, candidates in the merit list have been marked as:

  • Eligible
  • Does not fulfil non-creamy layer eligibility as per advertisement, hence not eligible
  • Candidate belongs to the SEBC category, hence not eligible
  • EWS certificate submitted is not of the requisite period
  • Domicile certificate not submitted, hence not eligible
  • Absent for document verification

2. Category-wise Select List

This section lists the candidates who have been provisionally selected against each reservation category, such as UR (Unreserved), SC, ST, OBC, VJ, NT(B), NT(C), NT(D), SEBC, EWS, and Women's Reservation (WR). Each entry includes the roll number, candidate's name, date of birth, applied category, total marks obtained, and the seat code under which they are selected (for example, UR-GEN, SC-GEN, OBC-GEN, UR-WR, SC-WR).

The select list also notes special provisions, such as candidates selected from the merit list as per Government of Maharashtra (GoM) guidelines in the absence of eligible sportsperson candidates under the sports quota.

3. Waiting List

A separate waiting list has been prepared category-wise (UR-GEN, SC-GEN, SC-WR, and other relevant categories). This list contains candidates next in line who may be considered for selection in case selected candidates do not join, fail document verification, or are found ineligible. Each waiting list entry shows the roll number, candidate name, date of birth, category, total marks, and wait-list rank/code (for example, UR-GEN-WL-1, SC-GEN-WL-2).

4. PWD (Persons with Disabilities) Category Note

The result document clarifies that no PWD candidate qualified under the specific PWD categories mentioned in the advertisement — namely, Specific Learning Disability/Mental Illness (1 post) and Multiple Disabilities of more than one type from one arm/one leg/leprosy cured/dwarfism/acid attack victims and specific learning disability/mental illness including deafness or hearing impairment (1 post). As a result, candidates as per the general merit list have been selected against these posts.

5. Marks of All Appeared Candidates

The final and largest section of the PDF lists the marks obtained by all 9,893 candidates who appeared for the online examination, out of 200 marks. For each candidate, the breakup is provided across four subjects — Marathi, English, General Knowledge, and Reasoning — along with Professional Knowledge marks, the total score, and the equated total (Eqt. Total) used for final ranking.

How to Check Your CIDCO Assistant Engineer (Civil) Result

This section explains the simple steps candidates can follow to locate their name and roll number in the CIDCO AE (Civil) result PDF.

  1. Open the official CIDCO result PDF for the Assistant Engineer (Civil) exam conducted on 21.07.2025.
  2. Use the search/find function (Ctrl+F) in the PDF to search for your roll number.
  3. Check the Merit List section to view your total marks and remarks status.
  4. If selected, your roll number will appear in the Category-wise Select List with a seat code such as UR-GEN, OBC-GEN, SC-WR, etc.
  5. If not selected, check the Waiting List section under your applicable category for your wait-list position.
  6. Refer to the "Marks of All Appeared Candidates" section for your subject-wise score breakdown.

Important Note for Selected and Waiting List Candidates

This section highlights the key conditions mentioned by CIDCO regarding the provisional nature of the result.

CIDCO has clearly stated that the select list and waiting list are purely provisional and subject to the production of original valid certificates and proofs, including:

  • Proof of required educational qualifications
  • Proof of additional qualifications, if any
  • Proof of age
  • Domicile certificate issued by a competent authority
  • Any other proof as required by law, as and where applicable.

AIIMS NORCET 10 Seat Allotment - How Are Seats Allocated?

Only candidates who successfully qualified in the NORCET 10 Stage II examination were considered for seat allocation.

Document Verification After Seat Allotment

The document verification stage is crucial because educational qualifications are verified, category claims are validated, nursing registration credentials are checked, and eligibility conditions are confirmed. Candidates preparing for the exam need clarity on exact shift timings to plan their reporting time at the centre. The OTET 2026 exam will be conducted on a single day, 28 June 2026, but in two separate shifts for the two papers.

Paper Exam Date Shift Timing
OTET Paper I 28 June 2026 (Sunday) 09:00 AM to 11:30 AM
OTET Paper II 28 June 2026 (Sunday) 02:00 PM to 04:30 PM

Candidates who have applied for both papers should plan their day carefully, since there is a gap between the morning and afternoon sessions.

Website Purpose

How to Download the OTET Admit Card 2026 PDF

This section explains the step-by-step process candidates need to follow to retrieve their hall ticket once the link is activated. The process is straightforward and requires only basic registration details.

  • Visit the official website at bseodisha.nic.in or bseodisha.ac.in

  • Exam date and shift timing
  • Exam centre name and address
  • Candidate's photograph and signature
  • Exam-day instructions

Candidates must arrive at the exam hall with a specific set of physical documents, since digital copies on a smartphone will not be accepted at the security checkpoint.

Document Type Requirement
Admit Card Clear printed copy of the OTET 2026 admit card

  • Carry the admit card along with a valid photo ID proof
  • Sit only at the seat assigned as per the admit card
  • Any use of unfair means will result in immediate cancellation of candidature
  • Follow all instructions given by the invigilator throughout the exam

  • Footwear such as slippers/sandals must be removed before entering.
  • Wearing any kind of jewellery is prohibited inside the exam centre.
  • Candidates will not be allowed to leave the exam hall during the first and last 30 minutes of the exam.

Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant Written Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant written exam pattern helps candidates prepare strategically. The examination is OMR-based and objective in nature, covering both technical and general aptitude topics. Here is the complete exam pattern for the Computer Assistant post.

  • Exam Mode: OMR-based (Objective Multiple Choice Questions)
  • Total Marks: 120 marks
  • Exam Duration: 2 hours (120 minutes)
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer

Subject-wise Marks Distribution - Computer Assistant

Subject / Section Maximum Marks Remarks
Technical Knowledge (Computer) 50 Marks Core technical paper
English Language Proficiency 20 Marks Counted in merit
General Knowledge 20 Marks Counted in merit
General Aptitude and Reasoning 10 Marks Counted in merit
Assamese Language Proficiency 20 Marks Qualifying only (minimum 8/20 required); not added to merit list

Important Note: The Assamese Language section is qualifying in nature. Candidates must score a minimum of 40% marks (8 out of 20) in this section to be eligible for the next stage. However, these marks will not be included when preparing the final merit list.

Candidates must carry their printed admit card along with a valid photo identity proof to the examination centre. Entry will be strictly denied without the hall ticket. The following documents are required on exam day:

Note: No TA/DA will be paid to candidates appearing in the written examination. Candidates are advised to report at the exam centre at least one hour before the scheduled exam time as mentioned on the admit card.

Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant Selection Process 2026

The selection for the Computer Assistant post under Gauhati High Court Recruitment 2026 is carried out in multiple stages. Candidates need to clear each stage to be considered for final appointment. The selection process consists of the following stages:

  1. Stage I - Written Examination: An OMR-based objective test of 120 marks and 2 hours duration. Candidates who clear the minimum qualifying marks in the Assamese section and secure sufficient marks overall proceed to the next stage.
  2. Stage II - Viva-Voce / Interview: Shortlisted candidates from the written examination are called for a personal interview or viva-voce test.
  3. Final Merit List: Based on the combined performance in the written test and viva-voce, a final merit list is prepared and selected candidates are appointed to the post of Computer Assistant.

This section covers the key timings for the upcoming APSC CCE Preliminary Examination. Candidates should note both sessions and plan their exam day accordingly.

Paper Session Timing
General Studies - Paper I Morning 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM
General Studies - Paper II Afternoon 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM

Candidates must report to their respective examination centres well before the reporting time mentioned on their admit cards. Late entry is generally not permitted.

APSC CCE Prelims 2026 - Exam Pattern Overview

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates stay focused during preparation. Here is a concise breakdown of how the APSC CCE Preliminary Examination is structured.

The Prelims exams consist of two objective-type papers (General Studies I and II), each of 200 marks with a duration of 2 hours and negative marking for wrong answers. 

Additional key facts:

  • Only GS Paper I marks are used for Prelims merit ranking. CSAT (Paper II) requires only 33% to qualify its marks are not counted for the Prelims merit list. 
  • Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applies in both Prelims papers. Unattempted questions carry zero penalty. 
  • There is no negative marking in the Mains (descriptive) exam or Interview stage.

APSC CCE 2026 Selection Process

The APSC CCE recruitment follows a three-stage selection process. Candidates must qualify each stage to advance to the next.

The selection process consists of three stages: the Prelims Exam, Mains Exam, and Interview. Here's what each stage involves:

Stage 1 - Prelims: Two objective-type papers (GS I + GS II), qualifying in nature. Only GS I marks count for merit.

Stage 2 - Mains: The Mains is a descriptive examination that includes an essay and multiple General Studies papers. It consists of 6 papers totalling 1,500 marks. 

Stage 3 - Interview (Personality Test): The final APSC cut-off list is made based on performance in the Mains Exam and Personality Test. The interview comprises a total of 180 marks, which contribute to the final merit list.

SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026 OUT - Download Hall Ticket at ssc.gov.in

SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026 has been released by the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) on 7 April 2026. Candidates who qualified in SSC CHSL Tier-I can now download their admit card from the official website ssc.gov.in (or respective regional SSC websites). The Tier-II examination (Descriptive + Skill Test) is scheduled for 10 April 2026 across various centers in India. This hall ticket is mandatory for appearing in the exam. Read below for the direct download link, step-by-step process, exam details, and important instructions for SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026.

How to Download SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026?

Follow these simple steps to download your SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026:

  1. Step 1: Visit the official SSC website at ssc.gov.in or click the direct download link provided above
  2. Step 2: Click on the “Admit Card” or “Download Admit Card” section (select your respective Regional SSC website if prompted)
  3. Step 3: Click on the link for “SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026”
  4. Step 4: Enter your credentials:
    • Registration Number / Roll Number
    • Password / Date of Birth (DD/MM/YYYY)
    • Captcha Code
  5. Step 5: Click on “Submit” or “Login” button
  6. Step 6: Your SSC CHSL Tier-II Admit Card 2026 will appear on screen
  7. Step 7: Download and save the PDF file on your device
  8. Step 8: Take 2-3 printouts for exam day (keep backup copies)

Pro Tip: Check all details on your admit card immediately after download. Report any discrepancies to the SSC helpdesk immediately.

SSC CHSL Tier 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 has been officially released on 1st April 2026 by the Staff Selection Commission (SSC). This slip provides qualified candidates (who cleared Tier-1) with advance information about their allotted exam city, exam date, and other preliminary details to help plan travel and accommodation. It is not the admit card. The SSC CHSL Tier 2 Admit Card 2026 will be released on 7th April 2026.

  • Release Date: 1st April 2026 (Released)

  • Exam Mode: Online CBT (Objective + Skill Test / Typing Test component)
  • Posts: Lower Divisional Clerk (LDC)/Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA), Postal Assistant/Sorting Assistant (PA/SA), Data Entry Operator (DEO) etc.

Direct Download Process (Step-by-Step Guide):

  1. Visit the official website: https://ssc.gov.in/
  2. Click on Candidate Login (or go to the dashboard section).
  3. Log in using your Registration Number (as Username) and Password (or Date of Birth as per your registration).
  4. Enter the captcha code.
  5. In the dashboard, look for the link “City of Examination”, “Exam City Details”, or “City Intimation Slip” for Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination 2025 (Tier-II).
  6. Your allotted exam city and related details will be displayed.

  • Shift Timing (if multiple shifts are conducted)

Note: The slip only mentions the exam city. The complete exam centre address, roll number, photo, signature, reporting time, and full guidelines will be available only in the Admit Card (releasing on 7th April 2026).

Critical Warning: You cannot enter the examination hall with only the city intimation slip. You must carry the admit card along with a valid original photo ID proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN, Passport, etc.).

What is SSC City Intimation Slip 2026?

The SSC City Intimation Slip 2026 is an advance notification document released before the admit card. It provides candidates with essential preliminary information about their examination to help them make necessary travel and accommodation arrangements. The city slip is NOT your admit card but serves as an important reference document.

Key Information Available in City Slip:

  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Shift timing (Shift 1: 9 AM - 10:30 AM, Shift 2: 12 Noon - 1:30 PM, etc.)
  • Reporting time at exam center
  • Gate closing time
  • Candidate's name and registration number
  • Category (SC/ST/OBC/General/EWS)
  • PwBD status (if applicable)

Important Notice: The city intimation slip is NOT your admit card and does not permit you to appear in the exam. It is only for informational purposes. You must download the admit card separately (from 1 February 2026 onwards) to enter the examination hall.

How to Download SSC City Intimation Slip 2026? (Step-by-Step Guide)

Step 1: Visit Official Website

  • Open your web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge recommended)
  • Visit SSC official website: ssc.gov.in
  • Ensure you have stable internet connection
  • On the homepage, look for “Admit Card/City Intimation” section or latest notices
  • Find link: “SSC MTS City Intimation Slip 2026” or “Check City Intimation for Multi-Tasking Staff and Havaldar Examination, 2025”
  • Click on the city intimation slip download link
  • You will be redirected to a candidate login page
  • Enter your Registration Number (Username)
  • Enter your Password or Date of Birth
  • Type the Captcha Code as shown in the image (case-sensitive)
  • Double-check all entered information for accuracy
  • Click on the “Login” or “Submit” button
  • Your city intimation slip will appear on the screen
  • Carefully verify all details displayed
  • Check: Name, Registration No., Exam City, Date, Shift Timing
  • Click on “Download” or “Save as PDF” button
  • Save the file to your computer/mobile device
  • Take a printout of the city slip for reference
  • Save a backup copy in cloud storage (Google Drive/Email)
  • Keep both digital and physical copies safe

Download your city intimation slip as soon as it is released to avoid server overload and last-minute technical issues. The website may experience heavy traffic during peak hours.

When you download your city intimation slip, you will find the following information:

Candidate Name Full name as per application form
Registration Number Unique registration ID
Exam Name Multi Tasking Staff and Havaldar Examination 2026
Exam City/State Name of city and state where exam center is located

The Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (HPPSC) has released 22 separate notifications (Advertisement Numbers 34/6-2026 to 55/6-2026, dated 17 June 2026) inviting Online Recruitment Applications (ORA) for 369 posts of Assistant Professor (College Cadre), Group-A (Job Trainee) in the Department of Higher Education, Himachal Pradesh. The last date to apply online and pay the fee is 14 July 2026 (11:59 PM), and selected candidates will draw a fixed Job Trainee emolument of Rs. 35,000 per month.

HPPSC Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026 - Quick Summary

Detail Information
Post Name Assistant Professor (College Cadre), Group-A (Job Trainee)
Organization Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (HPPSC)
Department Department of Higher Education, Himachal Pradesh
Total Vacancies 369 posts across 22 subjects

Last Date for Fee Payment 14 July 2026, 11:59 PM

Age Limit 18 to 45 years (as on 01-01-2026)

What Is the HPPSC Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026?

The HPPSC Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026 is a consolidated hiring drive covering 22 individual subject-wise advertisements for teaching positions in Himachal Pradesh's government colleges. Each subject, from Hindi and Chemistry to Tabla and Public Administration, has its own advertisement number but shares identical rules for age, fee, qualification pattern, and selection process. Candidates wondering whether this is one combined application or separate applications can note that each subject requires a separate Online Recruitment Application (ORA) on the HPPSC OTR portal, since vacancies, categories, and advertisement numbers differ subject to subject.

Subject-Wise Vacancy Breakdown (369 Posts)

Candidates looking for the exact vacancy count per subject can refer to the table below, which lists all 22 Assistant Professor posts advertised by HPPSC along with their advertisement numbers. The largest vacancy pools are in English (39 posts), Chemistry (34 posts), and Hindi (34 posts), while subjects like Tabla and Dance have only 2 posts each. All 369 posts carry the same pay of Rs. 35,000/- per month as Job Trainee under the Department of Higher Education.

Category-Wise Reservation Pattern

Each subject vacancy is further sub-divided into Unreserved (UR), SC, ST, OBC, and EWS categories of Himachal Pradesh, along with sub-quotas for Ex-Servicemen (Ex-SM), Ward of Freedom Fighters (WFF), and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (Hearing Impaired, Orthopedically/Physically Handicapped, Visually Impaired, and Intellectual or Multiple Disability) wherever applicable. For example, the English post (39 vacancies) breaks down as UR=16, SC=05, ST=03, OBC=02, EWS=04, with the remaining seats reserved for Ex-Servicemen and disability sub-categories, while smaller posts like Dance and Tabla (2 posts each) are fully unreserved. Candidates should check the post-specific category matrix in their relevant subject's official notification PDF before applying, since this can affect age relaxation and cut-off eligibility.

Important Dates for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates checking the HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 timeline can refer to the dates below, which apply uniformly across all 22 subject notifications. The notification was issued on 17 June 2026, and the online application window closes on 14 July 2026 at 11:59 PM, which is also the deadline for fee payment. Exam dates, admit card release, and result timelines have not yet been announced and will be notified separately on the official HPPSC website.

Last Date for Fee Payment 14 July 2026, 11:59 PM
Screening Test (CBT/Offline) & SAT Exam Date To be announced
Personality Test To be announced (held at HPPSC office, Shimla)

Eligibility Criteria for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates wondering about the qualification required for these posts can note that HPPSC has prescribed a uniform academic and age standard across all 22 subjects, with the subject of the Master's degree corresponding to the post applied for. The core requirement is a Master's degree with at least 55% marks (50% for SC/ST/OBC and PwBD candidates) in the relevant subject, along with a qualifying NET/SLET/SET score, and candidates must be between 18 and 45 years of age as on 1 January 2026.

Educational Qualification

  • A good academic record with at least 55% marks (or equivalent grade) at the Master's degree level in the relevant subject from a recognized Indian University, or an equivalent foreign degree recognized by the Government of India.
  • A 5% relaxation (55% to 50%) at the Master's level is available for SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer) candidates and for Physically/Visually Handicapped candidates.
  • A 5% relaxation is also available to Ph.D. holders who completed their Master's degree before September 1991.
  • Candidates must have cleared NET (UGC/CSIR) or an equivalent test accredited by HPPSC, such as SLET/SET, since NET/SLET remains the minimum eligibility condition for Assistant Professor recruitment.
  • Ph.D. holders are exempted from the NET/SLET/SET requirement, provided their Ph.D. was awarded in regular mode, evaluated by at least two external examiners, included an open viva-voce, and is supported by at least two published research papers (one in a refereed journal) plus two conference presentations from the Ph.D. work.
  • Candidates who qualified SET-2026 are also eligible to apply, and the application window will be reopened for them if the SET-2026 result is declared after the regular closing date.

Age Limit

The age limit for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 is fixed at 18 to 45 years, calculated as on 1 January 2026, based on the date of birth recorded in the candidate's Matriculation or equivalent certificate. A 5-year age relaxation in the upper limit is admissible only to Bonafide SC/ST/OBC of Himachal Pradesh, Ward of Freedom Fighters of HP, and Persons with Disabilities of HP, while HP Government employees and Ex-Servicemen of HP get relaxation as per separate government instructions. Importantly, this relaxation is available only if a post is reserved for that specific category in the subject being applied for.

Application Fee for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates asking how much the HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 application fee costs can note that it is a flat Rs. 600, charged uniformly irrespective of category or gender. The fee must be paid online through Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or other digital payment modes on the OTR portal before the closing date, and once paid, it is non-refundable under any circumstances and cannot be carried forward to another examination.

Category Application Fee
All Candidates (irrespective of category/gender) Rs. 600

Selection Process for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates curious about how HPPSC shortlists Assistant Professors can note that selection involves a two-paper written test on the same day followed by a Personality Test, with final merit based on the combined score of Paper-II and the interview. The process begins with document scrutiny and provisional admission, moves to the screening and aptitude tests, and concludes with a 30-mark Personality Test held at the Commission's office in Shimla.

Stage Component Details / Timeline Estimate
1 Application Scrutiny Eligible candidates provisionally admitted; rejected candidates get 10 days to represent
2 Paper-I: Screening Test 1-hour CBT/Offline MCQ test, 100 marks (GK of HP-30, National/International Affairs-30, Hindi-20, English-20); qualifying in nature
3 Paper-II: Subject Aptitude Test (SAT) 3-hour descriptive test, 120 marks, based on subject-specific syllabus; conducted same day as Paper-I
4 Document Verification Original documents checked for candidates shortlisted as per category-wise zone ratio (1:5 for 11+ posts; 1:5+3 for up to 10 posts)
5 Personality Test 30 marks, held only at HPPSC office, Shimla; minimum pass marks 40% (General) / 30% (Reserved)
6 Final Merit List Based on SAT (120) + Personality Test (30) = 150 marks total

Candidates should note that Paper-I is a qualifying screening test only and does not count toward final merit; candidates scoring zero or negative marks in Paper-I are excluded outright. There is negative marking of 0.25 marks for every wrong answer, multiple answers, or blank response in objective-type tests, and the minimum qualifying mark in the SAT is 45% for General category and 40% for reserved categories.

How to Apply for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates wondering how to submit their application can follow the numbered steps below, which apply to each subject's separate ORA on the HPPSC portal. The complete process is online, and once submitted, no corrections or modifications are allowed, so candidates must verify every field carefully before final submission.

  1. Visit the official HPPSC website at http://www.hppsc.hp.gov.in/hppsc.
  2. Click on the "Apply Online" link on the homepage.
  3. Select "One Time Registration (OTR) for Examinations" and complete "New Registration" if not already registered.
  4. Log in to the OTR account and view the list of live advertisements on the dashboard.
  5. Select the relevant subject advertisement (e.g., Hindi – 47/6-2026, History – 48/6-2026) and fill in the application form.
  6. Upload scanned copies of the required documents, including Matriculation certificate, degree/marksheets, category certificate, and Bonafide HP certificate.
  7. Pay the Rs. 600 application fee online via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or other digital mode.
  8. Give the undertaking confirming that uploaded documents are legible and readable, then submit the final application.
  9. Download or save the confirmation/printout for future reference.

Documents Required for Upload

Candidates preparing their application should keep the following documents ready in scanned format before starting the ORA, since applications without these uploads or with poor-quality scans are liable to rejection. The required documents include the Matriculation certificate for age proof, degree certificates with marksheets of all years, experience certificate (wherever required), and valid category certificates (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/WFF/PwBD) issued as per Himachal Pradesh Government's prescribed format. Reserved category candidates must additionally upload a Bonafide Himachali certificate, and EWS applicants need either an Income & Asset Certificate or a BPL Certificate countersigned by the BDO along with a non-SC/ST/OBC certificate.

Salary and Pay Scale for HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026

Candidates asking about the salary for this post can note that selected candidates will be engaged as Job Trainees on a fixed monthly emolument of Rs. 35,000, applicable uniformly across all 22 subjects. This pay structure follows the Department of Personnel's notification No. Per(AP)-C-B(15)-3/2024 dated 19 July 2025, which governs the scheme for engagement of job trainees on a fixed amount across Himachal Pradesh Government departments.

Post Pay Scale
Assistant Professor (College Cadre), Group-A, all 22 subjects Rs. 35,000/- per month (Job Trainee, fixed)

Common Mistakes Candidates Should Avoid

Many candidates lose their chance at selection due to avoidable errors during the application process rather than lack of qualification. Reviewing these common pitfalls before applying can help candidates submit a clean, error-free application on the first attempt.

  • Applying under the wrong subject advertisement number: Since there are 22 separate advertisement numbers (34/6-2026 to 55/6-2026), candidates sometimes apply to the wrong subject code, which cannot be corrected after submission.
  • Uploading low-resolution or unclear documents: HPPSC explicitly rejects applications where uploaded certificates are not legible, so scan documents at adequate resolution before uploading.
  • Submitting the application without final review: Once submitted, no corrections or modifications are permitted (except category change under specific rules), so double-check all entries, especially date of birth and category, before clicking submit.
  • Missing the NET/SLET/SET proof upload: Since NET/SLET/SET is the minimum eligibility condition, failing to upload valid qualifying certificates can lead to provisional rejection even if the candidate is otherwise eligible.
  • Ignoring the answer key objection window: Candidates who disagree with the Paper-I answer key must raise objections within 5 days of publication with the prescribed Rs. 100 fee per question; missing this window forfeits the right to challenge.
  • Not checking category-specific relaxation eligibility: Age and qualification relaxations apply only when a post is reserved for that category in the specific subject; assuming blanket relaxation without verifying the subject's category matrix can cause confusion later.

Eligibility criteria depend on the post and level. Candidates must meet educational, technical, and age requirements as per the Centralised Employment Notification.

  • Technician Grade I Signal: B.Sc. (Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / IT / Instrumentation) or Degree/Diploma in Engineering in relevant discipline from a recognized institution.
  • Technician Grade III: 10th / Matriculation plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in relevant trade or Act Apprenticeship in the concerned trade.
  • Other Conditions: Candidates must satisfy prescribed medical standards and citizenship norms and should be within the specified age limit as on the date mentioned in CEN 02/2026.

Age Limit

  • Technician Grade I Signal: 18 to 36 Years
  • Technician Grade III: 18 to 33 Years
  • Upper age relaxation for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/NCL/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/ PWBD) will be applicable as per Government of India rules and details will be given in the detailed CEN. 

Selection Process

RRB Technician recruitment involves multiple stages including a Computer Based Test and subsequent document and medical verification. There is no Computer Based Aptitude Test for these Technician posts.

  • Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Stage 2: Document Verification
  • Stage 3: Medical Examination

RRB Technician Exam Pattern 2026

  • Mode of Exam: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Total Questions: 100 Objective Type Questions
  • Total Marks: 100 Marks
  • Exam Duration: 90 Minutes
  • Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark will be deducted for each wrong answer; no negative marks for unattempted questions. 

Salary Details

  • Technician Grade I Signal: Pay Level 5 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 29,200/-
  • Technician Grade III: Pay Level 2 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 19,900/-
  • Additional allowances such as DA, HRA, TA and other benefits will be admissible as per Railway rules for the respective pay levels. 

How to Apply for RRB Technician Recruitment 2026

  • Visit your regional RRB website (e.g., Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Bengaluru, Chennai, Secunderabad, etc.).
  • Open the link for Centralised Employment Notification CEN 02/2026 – Technician.
  • Read the detailed notification carefully including post-wise eligibility, instructions and list of RRBs.
  • Register by providing basic details like name, mobile number and email ID.
  • Login using the registration credentials and fill the online application form for the desired post and pay level (only one RRB and one pay level allowed per candidate).
  • Upload required documents, photograph and signature as per specifications. >Pay the prescribed application fee through online mode, if applicable.
  • Submit the application form and take a printout / save PDF for future reference.

Important Points Mentioned in Indicative Notice

  • Each candidate can apply to only one RRB for a specific pay level and only one common online application is allowed for all notified posts in that pay level.
  • Separate applications must be submitted for each pay level, if eligible.
  • Candidates are strongly advised to verify name, date of birth and other details using Aadhaar to avoid mismatches at later stages.
  • RRBs caution candidates to be aware of touts, brokers and job racketeers and to rely only on official RRB websites for genuine information.

SSC CGL 2026 – Selection Process

Selection is through a two-tier Computer Based Examination (CBE). Marks scored in CBE conducted in multiple shifts will be normalized as per the procedure published by SSC vide Notice dated 02-06-2025. There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores at any stage.

Tier-I consists of Objective Type / MCQ questions, set in English and Hindi (except English Comprehension). Negative marking: 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II: Computer Based Examination

Tier-II is conducted in Paper-I, Paper-II, and Paper-III in separate shifts/days.

Negative marking in Tier-II: 1 mark per wrong answer in Section-I, II, III of Paper-I; 0.50 marks in Paper-II and Paper-III. Section-III (CKT) and Section-IV (DEST) are qualifying in nature. Candidates must qualify all sections of Paper-I separately. Higher standards of CKT and DEST are set for specific posts (CSS, MEA, AFHQ, SFIO, CBIC, Postal etc.). Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe.

SSC CGL 2026 – Exam Centres

The examination will be conducted through 9 SSC Regions covering all states and union territories. Candidates must choose three examination centres, in order of priority, within the same region.

No request for change of centre will be entertained after submission of the application. SSC may add, cancel, or shift candidates to another centre depending on administrative requirements.

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The multi-stage selection process will be adopted based on the number of applications received for each profile. Final selection is subject to document verification, performance in all selection stages, and Pre-Employment Medical Examination.

Stage 1 – Application Screening

Applications will be screened on the basis of years of relevant work experience, educational qualification, and other eligibility criteria as specified for each profile.

Stage 2 – Computer Based Test (CBT)

Part Section Details
Part I General Aptitude Verbal Ability, Quantitative Aptitude and Logical Reasoning
Part II Professional Knowledge Questions related to the area of specialization of the applied profile

Stage 3 – Case Based Discussion / Group Task / Personal Interview

Candidates shortlisted in the CBT (category-wise and discipline-wise merit list) will be called for Case Based Discussion and/or Group Task and/or Personal Interview. Document verification shall be conducted before this stage. Provisional selection will be based on relevant work experience, on-the-job achievements, and overall performance across all selection stages.

Stage 4 – Pre-Employment Medical Examination

Provisionally selected candidates must clear a Pre-Employment Medical Examination conducted by BPCL’s authorized doctor / nominated hospital as per OISD-GDN-166 guidelines. Medical fitness decision shall be final and binding. Reference for medical examination does not mean final selection.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Emoluments / Pay Scale

CTC includes Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (IDA pattern), HRA, Perks & Allowances, Retirement Benefits (DPE guidelines), and Performance-Related Pay. Additional benefits include medical coverage for self and dependants, annual leave entitlements, housing loan, education loan, furniture-on-hire, conveyance allowance, and communication expenses.

How to Apply for BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online only; no other mode of application will be accepted. Candidates must read the detailed advertisement carefully before applying. All details entered in the online form will be treated as final and no changes will be entertained after submission.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded (PDF format):

  • Date of Birth Proof (Class 10th / DOB Certificate)
  • Educational Qualification Proof - Consolidated Marksheet AND Degree / Diploma Certificate (both mandatory)
  • Service Certificate / Work-Experience Certificate(s) from each organization on their letterhead, signed/stamped by authorized representative, showing: Name, Designation, Length of Service, Date of Joining, Date of Separation (if applicable), Nature of Employment (Full-time / Part-time), Detailed Nature of Work, and Current Basic Salary and CTC
  • Relevant Category / Caste Certificate (SC / ST / OBC-NCL / EWS / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen) - issued for appointments under Government of India
  • Recent Color Passport Size Photograph (not older than April 2026)
  • Scanned copy of Signature (signature in CAPITAL LETTERS will NOT be accepted)
  • Latest three salary slips from current organization (scanned together in a single PDF file)

Additional Documents to be Produced at the time of Selection Process / Document Verification:

  • Call Letter / Admit Card along with a valid photo identity proof in original and self-attested photocopy
  • Caste Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for SC/ST candidates)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for OBC-NCL candidates); self-undertaking to be submitted at time of Personal Interview
  • Income and Asset Certificate issued by Competent Authority valid for FY 2026-27 (for EWS candidates); must be submitted at the time of interview
  • Disability Certificate issued by a Competent Authority as per RPwBD Act, 2016 (for PwBD candidates)
  • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from employer - mandatory for candidates presently employed in Central/State Government, Autonomous bodies, and PSUs

Apply Online at: www.bharatpetroleum.in → CAREERS → CURRENT JOB OPENING → APPLY ONLINE

For queries: Email - [email protected] (mention Application ID in the subject line). Candidates are NOT required to send printout of application or any other documents in hard copy to BPCL.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Important Instructions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • All eligibility criteria - age, qualification, and experience - are reckoned as on 01-04-2026.
  • Candidates can apply for only one profile. Candidates are advised to submit only one application; in case of multiple applications, only the latest one shall be considered as final.
  • Percentage of marks is calculated on the basis of total marks obtained in all semesters/years in all subjects. Rounding off of percentage is not allowed.
  • Experience gained only after the date of declaration of result of the qualifying degree will be considered. Short-term trainee experience (summer/winter internships during degree) will not be counted.
  • All qualifications must be from AICTE approved / UGC recognized University / Deemed University. Equivalent percentage for CGPA/OGPA must be indicated and supported by a certificate from the University.
  • OBC candidates belonging to ‘Creamy Layer’ are not entitled for OBC-NCL reservation; they must apply as General. OBC-NCL certificate should clearly indicate non-creamy layer status.
  • Candidates presently employed in Central / State Government, Autonomous bodies, PSUs must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer at the time of selection process.
  • All future communications will be through e-mail only. The email ID and mobile number must remain valid for at least one year. BPCL will not be responsible for non-delivery due to invalid email ID.
  • No email confirmation will be sent on successful registration or fee payment. Candidates must take a printout of the payment acknowledgment for future reference.
  • 3rd AC train fare reimbursement is admissible for CBT for outstation SC, ST & PwBD candidates. 2nd AC train fare is admissible for all outstation candidates appearing in the Interview (distance of not less than 30 km). This is not applicable for candidates already in Central / State Government Services / PSUs.
  • Corrigendum / Addendum, if any, will be published on the official BPCL website only - https://www.bharatpetroleum.in/ - candidates must check regularly.
  • BPCL reserves the right to cancel / restrict / enlarge / modify / alter the recruitment process at any stage without notice.
  • Canvassing in any form at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Court of jurisdiction for any dispute will be at Mumbai.
  • All applications are accepted through the online portal only. This activity has NOT been outsourced by BPCL to any agency/individual. Applicants are advised to beware of fraudulent agencies/individuals.

Qualification: Graduate (55% aggregate) + word processing/database/accounting proficiency + 5 years experience in Accounts/Purchase/Stores/General Admin. Knowledge of GFR and CPWD procurement procedures desirable. Age: Maximum 33 years.

TIFR Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The selection mode for TIFR 2026 varies by post category. TIFR Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply

Applications for TIFR Recruitment 2026 must be submitted online only at tifr.res.in. No offline or postal applications will be accepted. Government/Semi-Government/PSU employees, if called for the selection process, must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer.

  2. Navigate to the Careers / Recruitment section.
  3. Click on Advertisement No. 2026/6 and read the full notification carefully.
  4. Click "Apply Online" for the relevant post.
  5. Register and fill in all personal, educational, and experience details accurately.
  6. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature, and relevant certificates.
  7. Submit the online application before 4 July 2026.
  8. Take a printout of the completed application form for future reference.

Documents Required for TIFR Recruitment 2026

Candidates called for the selection process must bring originals along with copies of the following documents:

Salary & Appointment Terms

Candidates wondering about appointment duration can note that for posts at Sr. Nos. 1 to 7 and 12 to 17, the initial appointment will be for 3 years including a 1-year probation period. Continuation beyond 3 years is subject to comprehensive performance review; upon successful review, the appointment continues till superannuation at age 60. Post No. 30 (Project Administrative Assistant) is a temporary, non-pensionable contract appointment, renewable annually up to a total of 3 years. All other selected candidates (Posts 1-29) will be governed by the National Pension System (NPS) unless already covered under CCS (Pension) Rules 1972.

Candidates selected for posts at Sr. Nos. 12 to 17 and 22 to 29 will be required to work on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays and must be prepared for shift duties as per institutional requirements.

Who Should NOT Apply

  • Candidates who cannot produce grade-to-percentage conversion certificates from their university, where applicable.
  • Candidates already in government service who are unable to obtain an NOC from their employer before the selection stage.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

If you are a postgraduate with expertise in fields like Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security, Climate Finance, Quantum Technology, or Economic Research, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has opened a rare and prestigious opportunity. Under Advertisement No. RBI/TMD1/YP/06/2026-27/01 dated June 15, 2026, RBI is seeking 12 Young Professionals (YP) to work directly within its Central Office Departments (CODs) in Mumbai on short-to-medium-term policy assignments.

This is not an ordinary government job. The RBI Young Professional programme places selected candidates at the center of India's monetary policy, financial regulation, and technology governance framework. With a monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000, a contract tenure of up to 5 years, and direct exposure to top-level policy work, this engagement stands apart from conventional public sector roles.

The last date to apply is July 6, 2026. Applications must be submitted via email only.

  • [Apply Online] – Send your application to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] – Download the official notification: Advt. No. RBI/TMD1/YP/06/2026-27/01 from www.rbi.org.in

RBI Young Professional 2026 Overview

Before diving into the details, here is a complete quick-reference summary of the RBI YP Recruitment 2026 for candidates assessing their fit.

Detail Information
Organization Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Advertisement No. RBI/TMD1/YP/06/2026-27/01
Date of Notification June 15, 2026
Post Name Young Professional (YP)
Total Vacancies 12

Monthly Stipend ₹1,50,000 (fixed, subject to tax deductions)

Place of Posting Mumbai (Various Central Office Departments)
Application Mode Email only ([email protected])
Last Date to Apply July 6, 2026
Expected Joining August – October 2026 (Tentative)

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected YPs work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement is intended to enrich both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of the selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience in the Indian financial policy ecosystem.

All 12 Young Professional Positions – Post Codes, Job Areas, and Departments

This section lists every available Young Professional position in RBI's 2026 recruitment drive, along with the respective post code and the Central Office Department where the selected candidate will be placed.
