Post-wise Eligibility and Job Profiles: Complete Breakdown

Every RBI YP post has its own educational qualification requirements, desirable experience profile, and a distinct job profile. Understanding these differences is critical before applying. Applying for the wrong post or ignoring the post code in your email subject line could result in rejection.

1. YP0626DOS01 – Cyber Security and Information Technology Risk

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This role is designed for specialists who can help RBI assess technology risks, digital resilience, and cybersecurity threats across the regulated financial sector.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree or equivalent in Cyber Security / Information Security / Computer Science / IT / Data Science / AI or a related field.
  • Desirable Qualifications & Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CEH, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, AWS/Azure Security; published research in IT, Cybersecurity, or Public Policy journals.

Desirable Experience:

  • Cyber security, technology risk management, digital regulation, or fintech
  • Cloud security, cyber resilience, digital transformation projects
  • Experience with financial institutions, regulators, CERTs, or tech companies

What You Will Do: Conduct policy research on cyber security and digital resilience; draft framework documents; analyze cyber incidents and threat intelligence trends; support AI/ML, cloud security, and data governance projects.

2. YP0626DOS02 – Policy Analytics (DoS)

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This data-heavy role requires candidates who can transform complex supervisory data into actionable analytical outputs using advanced tools.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Computer Science/IT, or Master's degree in Statistics/Data Science.

Desirable Technical Skills:

  • Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot, VBA macros, automation)
  • Power BI (Advanced DAX, interactive dashboards, drill-through functionality)
  • Python (Pandas, NumPy, ETL workflows, automated reporting)
  • Statistics (regression analysis, forecasting, hypothesis testing, predictive modelling)
  • MIS Automation and large multi-source data management

What You Will Do: Extract and analyze supervisory datasets; develop Power BI dashboards; automate recurring MIS reports using VBA and Python; prepare analytical notes and policy briefs for senior management; support RTI/legal matters through structured data review.

3. YP0626DOR01 – Climate Change Risk and Sustainable Finance

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

With climate-related financial risks gaining regulatory prominence worldwide, this role positions the selected candidate at the frontier of ESG and sustainable finance regulation in India.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or PG qualification in Climate Change Studies / Environmental Science / Environmental Management / Climate Finance / Sustainability / Economics / Financial Economics / Finance / Statistics / Econometrics / Data Science / Public Policy / Disaster Management / Natural Resource Management / related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Certifications: FRM (GARP), SCR (GARP), ESG-related certifications.
  • Desirable Skills: Knowledge of physical and transition climate risks; understanding of ESG frameworks; Python, R, SQL, Excel, or data visualization tools.
  • What You Will Do: Climate risk research and analysis; policy support and regulatory framework development; climate stress testing; ESG and sustainable finance work; preparation of reports and policy notes; stakeholder engagement and capacity building.

4. YP0626DOR02 – Credit Risk Analytics & Regulatory Policy

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

This post is aimed at quantitatively strong candidates who can contribute to credit risk regulation, macroprudential analysis, and evidence-based policy development.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or equivalent in Economics / Econometrics / Statistics / Finance / Mathematics / Data Science / Financial Engineering or related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Qualification: PhD in Finance, Economics, or Statistics; or published research in credit risk or financial stability.
  • Desirable Experience: Risk modelling in financial institutions or credit rating agencies; experience with Python and large datasets; familiarity with ECL/IFRS-9, credit bureau data, BCBS and FSB regulatory standards.
  • What You Will Do: Frame and review credit risk regulations; identify regulatory gaps; support evidence-based policy; analyze international regulatory developments; develop analytical frameworks for assessing the impact of regulatory policies.

5. YP0626DPS01 – Payment Ecosystem

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This role calls for candidates who can track and analyze developments in India's rapidly evolving payment ecosystem, including cross-border payment architectures.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Payment systems, cross-border payments, public policy, or financial markets.

What You Will Do: Monitor market intelligence from international bodies (CPMI, FATF, BIS); undertake primary and secondary research on global payment architectures; generate analytical reports for international forums; statistical modelling of payment flow data.

6. YP0626DPS02 – Policy and Research in Domestic & Cross-Border Payment Systems

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This position supports RBI's top management with policy notes, research briefs, and market intelligence covering both domestic and international payment developments.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Public policy, payment systems.

What You Will Do: Prepare notes and briefs for RBI's top management on payment system policy; track domestic and international payment ecosystem developments; gather market intelligence from CPMI, FATF, BIS; contribute to research and thematic studies on payment systems.

7. YP0626DEP01 – Policy and Research (DEPR)

Department: Department of Economic and Policy Research, Central Office, Mumbai

This is one of the most academically demanding posts in the RBI YP 2026 recruitment, designed for candidates with strong economics research credentials.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's or PhD in Economics, with at least one course paper in Mathematics, Statistics, or Econometrics during the Master's programme.
  • Desirable Qualification: Authored at least one paper in a reputed journal ranked B or above.
  • Desirable Experience: Economic research; experience with STATA, EViews, Python, or R.
  • What You Will Do: Review research papers and reports on policy and regulatory matters; prepare concise summaries and background notes for RBI's top management; support senior leadership in meetings and presentations.

8. YP0626FIN01 – Artificial Intelligence

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

As AI transforms the financial sector, RBI seeks a specialist who can shape its approach to AI governance, ethics, and regulatory oversight.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in AI / Computer Science / Public Policy / Data Science or a related discipline.
  • Desirable Knowledge: AI governance, machine learning concepts, data ethics, emerging technology policy frameworks.
  • Desirable Experience: AI research, technology policy, data analysis; exposure to ethical AI frameworks, regulatory research, or public policy projects.
  • What You Will Do: Analyse emerging AI technologies; develop policy recommendations on ethics, governance, data privacy, and responsible AI adoption; support regulatory research and stakeholder consultations; assist in strategy formulation for AI-driven innovation ecosystems.

9. YP0626FIN02 – Quantum Technology

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This highly specialized and forward-looking role places a candidate at the cutting edge of India's quantum technology policy landscape.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in Quantum Computing / Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / Technology Policy.
  • Desirable Knowledge: Quantum technologies, cybersecurity implications, innovation policy research.
  • Desirable Experience: Quantum technology research, emerging technology analysis, quantum computing applications, or cybersecurity research.
  • What You Will Do: Conduct research on quantum computing, communication, and cybersecurity trends; assist in developing strategic frameworks for quantum ecosystem development; support standards-setting and international collaboration initiatives.

10. YP0626FMO01 – Data Analysis

Department: Financial Markets Operations Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role suits a candidate who can translate financial market data into policy-relevant insights, particularly in the money market domain.

  • Essential Qualification: Post Graduation in Statistics / Economics with Econometrics as a subject.
  • Desirable Qualifications: CFA, FRM; proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Desirable Experience: Econometrics; published research; banking dealer experience; money market exposure.
  • What You Will Do: Perform data analysis to support policy research; track domestic and global currency and yield movements; analyze money market rates on a daily basis.

11. YP0626FMR01 – Financial Markets

Department: Financial Markets Regulation Department, Central Office, Mumbai

A role for quantitatively oriented professionals who can harness analytical tools to study and interpret financial market behavior for regulatory purposes.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree in Economics / Operations Research / Finance / Statistics / Mathematics.
  • Desirable Experience: Any area related to financial markets.
  • What You Will Do: Study and analyze financial market data using cutting-edge analytical tools in close coordination with the regulatory function.

12. YP0626CEP01 – Data Analytics and Policy Research

Department: Consumer Education and Protection Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role focuses on using data science and machine learning to understand consumer complaint trends and translate them into policy inputs for RBI's leadership.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech, or Postgraduate degree in Mathematics / Statistics / Computer Science / Economics / Data Analytics with knowledge of statistical tools and Power BI.
  • Desirable Skills: Python, R, or SQL for automation, machine learning, and large dataset handling.
  • What You Will Do: Data mining and analytics using AI/ML tools; systematic classification of consumer complaints and trends; process automation of report generation; development of interactive real-time dashboards; preparation of quality policy inputs for RBI's top management.

Who Can Apply? General Eligibility Criteria for RBI YP 2026

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

How to Apply for RBI Young Professional 2026 – Step-by-Step

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 – Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 – Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 – Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 – Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application – [Post Code] – [Your Full Name]"
Example: YP Application – YP0626FIN01 – Ramesh Kumar

Step 5 – Send the Application:
Email your complete application to [email protected] before the deadline.

Step 6 – Applying for Multiple Posts:
If you wish to apply for more than one position, send a separate email for each post. Each email must include a complete, independent set of all required documents.

  • [Apply Online] – Send your application email to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] – Download the official notification and Annexure-VI application proforma from www.rbi.org.in

Last Date: July 6, 2026

Selection Process for RBI YP 2026

Submitting a complete and eligible application is only the first step. The selection process for RBI Young Professionals involves multiple stages, and meeting the minimum eligibility is not a guarantee of progression.

Stage 1 – Preliminary Screening: A screening committee reviews all received applications against the eligibility criteria and the quality of supporting documents. The Bank reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview.

Stage 2 – Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit and verify original documents related to age, educational qualifications, and experience.

Stage 3 – Interview: Shortlisted candidates will receive an interview call letter via email only. No physical call letters will be sent by post. Candidates must make their own travel and accommodation arrangements for the interview.

Reserve List: RBI maintains a reserve list of suitable candidates, valid for one year from the date of publication of the selection list.

RBI's decision regarding shortlisting, interview, and all aspects of engagement is final. No correspondence will be entertained in this regard.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a university recognized by the Government of India. Graduation must have been completed on or after January 1, 2022. Mark sheets and provisional/degree certificates will be required at the time of verification.

NATS Registration Requirement

Candidates must be registered on the NATS portal (https://nats.education.gov.in) to be eligible to apply. Registration on the government apprenticeship portal is a mandatory prerequisite.

Other Key Eligibility Conditions

  • Candidates must not have previously undergone or be currently pursuing any apprenticeship under the Apprentices Act, 1961 in any organization, including Central Bank of India.
  • Candidates who have completed one year or more of training or job experience after attaining their educational qualification are not eligible.
  • No Ex-servicemen or Disabled Ex-Servicemen are eligible, and no reservation is provided for them.

Central Bank of India Apprentice Vacancy 2026 - State-wise Distribution

The 4,500 training seats are distributed across all states and union territories. The major states by number of seats are listed below. Complete district-wise breakdowns are available in Annexure I of the official notification.

Application Fee for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The fee is non-refundable and must be paid online. GST at 18% is charged additionally on the base fee.

PwBD (Any Category) Nil ₹200 ₹236

Payment is accepted through online mode only. No other payment method is accepted. Fee once paid is not refunded under any circumstances.

How to Apply for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The application process involves two portals. Here is a step-by-step guide:

Step 1 - Register on NATS Portal Visit https://nats.education.gov.in and navigate to the "Student Register/Login" section. Complete your registration and note your Enrolment ID, which is required for all future correspondence.

Step 2 - Find CBI Apprenticeship on NATS After logging in, visit https://nats.education.gov.in/student_type.php to find and apply to the Central Bank of India apprenticeship advertisement.

Step 3 - Complete Application on BEEP Portal After applying on NATS, you will receive an email from BFSI SSC ([email protected]) with a link to register on https://beep.bfsissc.com. Complete your final application here by entering caste category, district preferences, and other details.

Step 4 - Pay the Application Fee Pay the applicable fee online through the BEEP portal. The application is complete only after successful payment.

Step 5 - Save Your Application Take a printout of the system-generated online application form after submitting. Do not make multiple submissions; only the last valid completed application will be retained.

Selection Process for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Selection involves multiple stages. Candidates must clear all stages to be engaged as apprentices.

Stage 1 - Online Written Examination

The exam is objective type, conducted by BFSI SSC. It will be taken from the candidate's own home on their own device - no admit card or examination centre is required.

Subject Questions Marks Duration
General / Financial Awareness 20 20 -
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 20 20 -
Computer Knowledge 20 20 -
General English 20 20 -
Central Bank of India Products & Services 20 20 -
Total 100 100 60 minutes
  • Medium: English/Hindi (General English section in English only)
  • No negative marking for wrong answers
  • Tie-breaking rule: if two candidates score equally, the older candidate ranks higher (descending order of age)
  • Details on CBI Products & Services will be shared on the bank's official website in due course

Stage 2 - Test of Local Language

Candidates must be proficient (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified official language of the state they apply for. This test is conducted after qualifying the online exam at a centre decided by the bank, at the candidate's own expense.

Candidates who have studied the specified local language at the 10th or 12th standard level (as evidenced by mark sheets) are exempt from the language test.

Stage 3 - Document Verification

Qualified candidates are called to the relevant CBI Regional/Zonal Office for verification of all original documents, including date of birth proof, graduation certificates, category certificates, and any other relevant documents.

Stage 4 - Medical Fitness Verification

Final engagement is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit by a qualified medical practitioner or MBBS doctor, as per the bank's requirements.

Stipend, Training Conditions, and Benefits

Understanding what to expect during the apprenticeship helps candidates plan ahead.

  • Monthly Stipend: ₹15,000 per month for the 12-month training period
  • No other allowances or employee benefits are provided
  • Leave: One casual leave per month; public/bank holidays as applicable; no other leave types
  • Working hours: Same as clerical staff of the bank; no overtime is permitted
  • No hostel, transport, or residential accommodation is provided by the bank
  • An assessment test may be conducted after completion, followed by certification as per prevailing guidelines
  • Apprentices are trainees, not employees - no labour laws or employee benefits apply
  • Apprentices cannot form or join any union

Contract of Apprenticeship

Candidates selected after document verification will receive a digital apprenticeship contract through the NATS government portal (https://nats.education.gov.in). They must accept the contract within the stipulated timeframe. No candidate can begin training without an approved apprenticeship contract.

Termination Conditions

The contract may be terminated in the following situations:

  • Non-reporting on the date of commencement of On-Job Training
  • Automatic termination on expiry of the 12-month training period
  • Mutual application to the Apprenticeship Advisor (BFSI SSC) before completion, with stated reasons
  • Misconduct by the apprentice, with written notice from the bank
  • If the Apprenticeship Advisor finds either party has failed to fulfil the contract terms

Documents Required at the Time of Document Verification

Candidates must carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of all the following:

  • System-generated printout of online application/NATS enrolment form
  • Date of Birth proof (Birth Certificate or Class X certificate with DOB)
  • Photo identity proof
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and final degree certificate
  • Caste certificate (for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates) in the Government of India prescribed format
  • OBC certificate must explicitly contain the non-creamy layer clause and be valid as on the date of the Language Test (issued within one year)
  • Disability certificate from District Medical Board (for PwBD candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates) issued by competent authority

Reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Under Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, reservation for PwBD is on a horizontal basis within the overall vacancies for each state. The qualifying disability categories include:

  • Visual Impairment (Blindness and Low Vision)
  • Hearing Impairment (Deaf and Hard of Hearing)
  • Orthopedic/Locomotor Disability (OA, OL, BL, OAL)
  • Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism, Acid Attack Victims, Muscular Dystrophy
  • Intellectual Disability (Autism Spectrum Disorder, Specific Learning Disability, Mental Illness)
  • Multiple Disabilities

A total of 45 seats each are reserved for VI, HI, OH, and ID categories, amounting to 180 PwBD seats across the country.

Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) Eligibility

Candidates not covered under SC/ST/OBC reservation and whose family gross annual income is below ₹8 lakh from all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession) qualify for EWS reservation. Additionally, the family must not own:

  • 5 acres or more of agricultural land
  • A residential flat of 1,000 sq. ft. or more
  • A residential plot of 100 sq. yards or more in notified municipalities
  • A residential plot of 200 sq. yards or more outside notified municipalities

The EWS benefit requires an Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed Government of India format, issued by a competent authority.

Where to Find Updates and Announcements

All announcements, addendums, and corrigenda will be published exclusively on:

  • Central Bank of India official website: Click here (Career section → Current Opportunities)
  • BFSI SSC portal: https://bfsissc.com
  • BEEP portal: https://beep.bfsissc.com (under "My Applied Opportunities")

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi has released the Detailed Recruitment Advertisement for Common Recruitment Examination-5 (CRE-5) on 11 June 2026. The examination invites applications from eligible Indian nationals for a wide range of Non-Faculty Group-B and Group-C posts spread across 28 participating AIIMS and Central Government Institutes/Bodies. The last date to apply online is 30 June 2026 (up to 5:00 PM) at www.aiimsexams.ac.in. The Computer Based Test (CBT) is tentatively scheduled for 25 to 27 July 2026.

About CRE-5: What Is It and Who Is It For?

CRE-5 is a unified, single-window recruitment platform that allows eligible candidates to apply once and be considered for similar posts across multiple participating institutes. The Examination Section, AIIMS New Delhi acts solely as the examination-conducting body; recruitment rules, service conditions, and final appointment decisions rest entirely with each participating institute independently.

Participating organizations are autonomous bodies or subordinate offices under the Government of India, functioning independently from AIIMS New Delhi. Candidates are advised to check each institute's individual recruitment rules and eligibility criteria before applying, as conditions may differ for the same post name across different institutes.

Participating Institutes (28 Total)

AIIMS Awantipora, AIIMS Bathinda, AIIMS Bhopal, AIIMS Bibinagar, AIIMS Bilaspur, AIIMS Deoghar, AIIMS Gorakhpur, AIIMS Guwahati, AIIMS Kalyani, AIIMS Mangalagiri, AIIMS Madurai, AIIMS Nagpur, AIIMS New Delhi, AIIMS Patna, AIIMS Raebareli, AIIMS Raipur, AIIMS Rajkot, AIIMS Rewari, AIIMS Rishikesh, AIIMS Vijaypur, AIIMS-CAPFIMS (New Delhi), Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences & Dr. RML Hospital, Chittaranjan National Cancer Institute (CNCI) Kolkata, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Lady Hardinge Medical College & associated Sucheta Kriplani Hospital and Kalawati Saran Children's Hospital, Pasteur Institute of India, Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC) Najafgarh, and Regional Institute of Paramedical and Nursing Sciences (RIPANS) Aizawl.

However, application fees paid by SC/ST candidates who appear in the examination will be refunded to the source account after declaration of results.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern and Syllabus

The CRE-5 Computer Based Test is a structured, time-bound examination designed to assess both domain knowledge and general aptitude.

CBT Structure

Parameter Detail
Duration 90 minutes
Total Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 400 marks (4 marks per question)
Negative Marking –1 mark per wrong answer (1/4th deduction)
General Knowledge & Aptitude / Computer 20 MCQs
Domain-Specific Questions 80 MCQs
Sections 5 sections × 20 questions × 18 minutes each

Each section is sequential and time-locked - once a section closes, candidates cannot return to it. Candidates must attempt all possible questions within the active section's time window.

Medium of Examination

Posts where the essential qualification is 10th/12th will be examined in bilingual (English and Hindi) medium. Posts requiring bachelor's or higher qualifications, or posts involving specific technical domain knowledge, will be examined in English only.

Qualifying Marks

Category Qualifying Percentage
UR / EWS 40%
OBC 35%
SC / ST 30%
PwBD (all categories) 30%
Ex-Servicemen As per their category

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) higher marks in the domain-specific section; (ii) fewer wrong answers/negative marks; (iii) older date of birth; (iv) alphabetical order of name, then father's name, then mother's name.

Full syllabus details for all 57 groups are in Section IX of the official DRA.

Skill Test

For selected post groups, a Skill Test is conducted as Stage II for candidates who qualify the CBT. The skill test is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared based on CBT performance, but only among those who pass the skill test for the relevant post.

Posts requiring skill tests include groups such as Junior Administrative Assistant (typing test), Stenographer (stenography test), Programmer (computer skill test), Hindi Translator (translation test), Assistant Security Officer (PST), and Fire Technician (PET & PST). See Annexure-V of the DRA for complete scheme details.

If a candidate qualifies the CBT but fails the skill test, they remain eligible only for posts within the same group that do not require a skill test.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

CRE-5 follows a multi-stage recruitment process. Each stage is mandatory for progression to the next.

Stage 1 - Online Application: Candidates register on www.aiimsexams.ac.in and submit applications by 30 June 2026.

Stage 2 - Application Acceptance: Application status published on 9 July 2026.

Stage 3 - Computer Based Test (CBT): Tentatively 25–27 July 2026 at examination centres across major states/UTs of India.

Stage 4 - Skill Test (where applicable): Conducted after CBT for qualifying candidates in applicable groups. Venue: preferably Delhi/NCR. Date to be notified.

Stage 5 - Choice & Preference: Qualified candidates are invited to exercise institute choices and indicate order of preference. Candidates who fail to exercise choices within the given period will not be considered for any institute.

Stage 6 - Seat Allocation: Allocation is made in order of merit based on choices exercised and eligibility at each participating institute.

Stage 7 - Document Verification: Original certificates verified by the respective AIIMS/Institute on the date notified by them.

Stage 8 - Joining: Selected candidates must report on the date specified in the result/allocation notice. Failure to report will lead to mandatory cancellation of candidature for CRE.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Salary / Pay Scale

Pay scales follow the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix. Specific pay levels differ by post and institute.

Pay Level 3 ₹21,700/month Library Attendant Grade II
Pay Level 4 ₹25,500/month Cashier, Dispensing Attendant, Data Entry Operator Grade A, Electrician, Assistant Laundry Supervisor
Pay Level 5 ₹29,200/month Warden (RHTC), Pharmacist, Technologist (OT), Junior Medical Lab Technologist, Operation Theatre Assistant, Manifold Technician (Gas Steward)
Pay Level 6 ₹35,400/month Assistant Dietician, Junior Administrative Officer, Assistant (ICMR), Junior Engineer (Civil/Electrical), Store Keeper, Junior Accounts Officer, Technical Assistant (OT/MLT)
Pay Level 7 ₹44,900/month Dietician, Assistant Engineer (Civil/Electrical/AC&R), Librarian Grade I

In addition to basic pay, posts carry allowances (HRA, DA, TA, etc.) as per the rules applicable at each respective institute.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply for AIIMS CRE-5 2026

Applications can only be submitted through the Online Registration Terminal (OTR) at www.aiimsexams.ac.in. Physical documents must not be sent; no correspondence regarding correction in registration will be entertained.

  1. Visit the official website: www.aiimsexams.ac.in
  2. Register through the OTR (One-Time Registration) portal if you have not already done so.
  3. Log in and select the CRE-5 application link.
  4. Fill in all details carefully - name, date of birth, category, qualification, experience, and NOC details if applicable.
  5. Upload photographs, signature, and left thumb impression in the format specified under "Upload Image Instructions."
  6. Select your examination centre preference (state/UT).
  7. Pay the applicable examination fee via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
  8. Submit the application and download the registration slip for your records.
  9. If you are working in a Government/PSU/Autonomous Body, upload the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from your current employer by 6 July 2026 - failing to do so will prevent you from appearing in the examination.
  10. Check your application status on 9 July 2026 at www.aiimsexams.ac.in.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Required Documents and Certificates

Candidates must have all certificates ready at the time of applying, as no additional time will be granted at document verification. Documents required include:

  • Downloaded Registration Slip and Admit Card
  • Date of Birth certificate (Matriculation certificate or equivalent)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) - valid and current; OBC NCL certificate must be valid for Financial Year 2026-27 (issued on or after 01 April 2026)
  • EWS certificate issued between 01 April 2026 and 30 June 2026
  • Disability certificate (for PwBD candidates, with minimum 40% benchmark disability)
  • No Objection Certificate from current employer (for Govt./PSU/Autonomous Body employees)
  • Educational qualification certificates
  • Experience certificates mentioning dates, basic pay, and nature of duties
  • Any other certificate required by the respective institute

BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

All candidates will undergo the recruitment process in the following sequence: (i) Written Examination, (ii) Physical Efficiency Test (PET) including physical measurements and Trade Test (TT) where applicable, (iii) Primary Medical Examination (PME) and Document Verification (DV), and (iv) Induction/Joining. The PET and TT are qualifying in nature - final merit is based solely on written exam marks, subject to qualifying PET, TT, and clearing PME. Minimum passing marks in written exam: 50% for UR/EWS/OBC; 40% for SC/ST. Trade test requires minimum 40% marks to qualify.

Physical Efficiency Test (PET): Candidate must complete 1.6 km (1 mile) run in 10 minutes. PwBD, ESM, Ex-Agniveers, and departmental re-appointment candidates are exempt from PET.

Competition Level Analysis for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

The competition level for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 is expected to be moderate to high. The recruitment is restricted to Male candidates only, which reduces the applicant pool compared to open-gender recruitments. However, 899 vacancies across technical/trade posts will attract a large number of ITI-qualified and Matriculation-level candidates, especially for high-vacancy posts like Store Keeper Technical (300) and Operator Communication (261). The written exam followed by PET and Trade Test provides multiple elimination stages, but candidates with relevant ITI trade certificates and physical fitness will have a clear advantage. Ex-Servicemen and Ex-Agniveers get significant age relaxation and weightage, which makes certain trades more competitive in that segment.

The key differentiator here is the offline application process - many eligible candidates may miss out due to postal delays or incorrect application format, effectively reducing actual competition at the written exam stage. Candidates who submit complete and correct applications well before the deadline and prepare trade-specific written exam syllabi will have a significant edge.

Who should NOT apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Female candidates - this recruitment is strictly for Indian National Males only.
  • Candidates who do not possess the requisite educational/technical qualification as on the closing date of application; those awaiting final exam results are not eligible.
  • Candidates outside the age band 18-27 years as on 01 Jun 2026 (except those eligible for applicable category-based relaxation).
  • OBC candidates from the Creamy Layer - they are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply as UR/General category.
  • Candidates who cannot meet the region-wise physical standards (height, chest, weight) as physical fitness is mandatory for induction.
  • Candidates with permanent medical conditions listed as grounds for permanent rejection (colour blindness for Drivers/Operators, cardiac conditions, gross myopia, etc.) who cannot pass the Primary Medical Examination at GREF Centre.
  • Candidates unwilling or unable to be posted anywhere in India, especially in remote, high-altitude, or difficult terrain areas in Northern and Eastern regions.
  • Candidates who cannot arrange and send a physical application form with photograph, thumb impression, signature, fee e-receipt, and attested copies by post to Pune - there is no online application mode.
  • Candidates with tattoos on any body part other than the inner forearm (inside elbow to wrist) or reverse palm - tattoos on other parts lead to disqualification at PME.
  • Ex-servicemen who have already joined Govt civil service using ESM benefits and are claiming ESM status again - such candidates are treated as civilian employees.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Not printing the application form on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card on both sides of a single paper as mandated - non-standard paper leads to rejection.
  • Applying without attaching the e-receipt copy of the application fee paid via SBI Collect; no other payment mode is accepted and missing receipt causes rejection.
  • Sending the application from a wrong/old address instead of present postal address - applications posted from wrong address are rejected to prevent fraudulent claims of 60-day receipt benefit.
  • Not superscribing the envelope with "APPLICATION FOR (NAME OF TRADE/POST) Under Category (UR/SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM/CPL)" as required - unlabelled envelopes may be misdirected.
  • Mismatch between name in application and name in Matriculation certificate - even a dropped or added part of the name requires a Gazette Notification; otherwise candidature is summarily cancelled.
  • Submitting multiple applications for the same post with different details or photographs - this results in lifetime debarment from all GREF examinations.
  • OBC/EWS certificate dated older than one year from the closing date - OBC and EWS certificates must be fresh (not older than one year as on closing date) and in the prescribed Central Govt format.
  • Candidates applying for more than one post/trade using the same envelope - each post requires a separate application with separate fee in a separate envelope.
  • Not carrying the minimum 12 passport-size photographs (same as pasted on application and admit card) to all subsequent recruitment stages - shortage of photos causes disruption at PET/TT/PME stages.
  • Ignoring the trade-specific syllabus and treating the written exam as a general knowledge test - each post has a distinct subject-wise syllabus and candidates must prepare trade-specific topics.

How to Apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply offline only; no online application mode is available. Application form and admit card must be downloaded from the official BRO website (www.bro.gov.in) and filled in English or Hindi only, in capital letters. The application form must be printed on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card printed on both sides of a single paper. Candidates must first pay the application fee online via SBI Collect portal and attach the e-receipt copy. Candidates applying for more than one post must send separate applications with separate fee in separate envelopes. Candidates are strongly advised to send applications well before the closing date and not wait for the last day - GREF Centre will not be responsible for postal delays.

Candidates should read the detailed instructions and guidelines available at https://bfsissc.com before applying.

Documents Required to be Enclosed with Application Form:

  • Recent colour passport-size photograph (not older than 1 month from the date of Advertisement) pasted at the prescribed place on application form and admit card - minimum 12 copies of the same photograph to be carried throughout the recruitment process
  • Left hand thumb impression at the prescribed place on application form and admit card
  • Signature of candidate at the prescribed place
  • Copy of e-receipt of application fee paid via SBI Collect
  • Self-attested photostat copies of certificates for essential educational/technical qualifications (Matriculation onwards), date of birth, caste certificate (as per format in Appendix A/B), OBC NCL declaration (Appendix D), EWS certificate (Appendix C), Disability Certificate (Appendix E for PwBD), experience certificate (if applicable), Driving Licence copy (for OEM post)
  • NCC certificate copies (B or C grade), sports certificate, or relationship certificate for Sons of Serving/Ex-GREF personnel - for claiming weightage marks
  • Proof of residence/domicile (for correct physical standards region)
  • Any certificate in language other than Hindi or English must be enclosed with an attested Hindi/English translation by a Group A Gazetted Officer

Send Application (by Postal Service) to: Commandant, GREF Centre, Dighi Camp, Pune - 411015

Printout / physical application is NOT to be sent anywhere else. No hard copy of admit card for written exam will be sent by post - admit card will be posted to the communication address given by the candidate in the admit card.

Application form available at: https://www.bro.gov.in

For queries: Visit https://www.bro.gov.in - all recruitment updates, results, and call letters will be displayed on the BRO website only.

Important Instructions for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • Only Male Indian Nationals can apply; Female candidates are not eligible.
  • Application form and/or admit card without signature, without photograph, or without thumb impression will be summarily rejected - no communication will be done for rejected applications.
  • Candidates must ensure their Aadhaar Card photo is current (not older than 2-3 years from written exam date) and address/phone is updated; outdated Aadhaar may prevent entry to the exam.
  • Son of Serving / Ex-GREF staff should write father's GS No., Rank, and Name on top of the application in red ink with a photocopy of relationship certificate, to claim the 15% weightage benefit.
  • Casual Paid Labours (CPL) of GREF who have worked for 179 days in the last one year and are on the Muster Roll on the date of advertisement publication get 10% additional weightage - attach experience certificate signed by OC unit, countersigned by Commander BRTF and verified by Accounts Officer.
  • SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates who qualify on their own merit (without relaxed standards) will be accommodated against UR vacancies - they must NOT apply separately against UR vacancies.
  • OBC candidates belonging to Creamy Layer are not entitled to reservation; they should apply under UR category.
  • Candidates serving in other Government Departments must apply through proper channel sufficiently in advance; applications not received by due date through proper channel will be rejected.
  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, and all electronic/communication devices are strictly NOT ALLOWED inside GREF Centre, Pune campus during any recruitment process.
  • A candidate who absents himself during any recruitment activity for which he has been called will have his candidature cancelled automatically - he will not be allowed to appear for further stages.
  • There shall be no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores in examination; no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this Advertisement shall fall within the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
  • Impersonation or submission of forged documents leads to debarment from all GREF examinations for life/2 years and legal action. GREF has not appointed any agent or coaching centre for action on its behalf - SELECTION WILL BE DONE PURELY ON MERIT IN A TRANSPARENT MANNER.
  • Vacancies are liable to increase/decrease/cancel at any stage without notice due to unforeseen situations.
  • All revisions/corrigendum will be hosted on the BRO website only - candidates should visit www.bro.gov.in regularly.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Vacancy Details

A total of 60 vacancies have been announced for Permanent Commission in Technical Branches of the Indian Navy. Candidates must give their preference of Mechanical Engineering or Electronics & Communication Engineering during online application. Based on merit and qualification during training at INA, 07 candidates from Mechanical Engineering will be streamed to B.Tech in Naval Architecture & Shipbuilding at NCW, Kochi. Vacancies are tentative and may be changed depending on service requirements. Multiple applications by any candidate will lead to cancellation of candidature.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfill all eligibility conditions as on the date of application. Only unmarried men and women fulfilling the conditions of nationality as laid down by the Government of India are eligible. Any candidate found to be married or who marries while under training will be discharged from service and shall be liable to refund full training cost including pay, allowances and any other expenditure incurred by the Government.

Criteria Details
Nationality As per conditions of nationality laid down by the Government of India.
Marital Status Unmarried men and women only. Candidates who marry while under training will be discharged and must refund all training costs.
Educational Qualification Passed Senior Secondary Examination (10+2 pattern) or equivalent from any recognized Board with at least 70% aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM) and at least 50% marks in English (either in Class X or Class XII).
JEE (Main) 2026 Requirement Must have appeared for JEE (Main) 2026 exam (for B.E./B.Tech). Call up for SSB will be issued on the basis of JEE (Main) All India Common Rank List (CRL) 2026 published by NTA. Candidates must fill their CRL Rank in the application.
Medical Standards All candidates recommended by SSB must undergo medical examination applicable to 10+2 (B.Tech) entry. Candidates already declared medically fit for NDA/INA Jan 27 need not repeat medical examination. No relaxation in medical standards on any grounds. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.
Narcotics Use/possession of narcotics is banned. Candidates may be tested during SSB/medicals/training/service. If found using/possessing narcotics at any stage, candidate will be debarred from joining or removed from service.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Age Limit

Candidates must have been born between 02 July 2007 and 01 January 2010 (both dates inclusive) to be eligible for the January 2027 course. There is no separate age relaxation mentioned — the age band is fixed for all candidates.

Category Age Band
All candidates (Men and Women) Born between 02-07-2007 and 01-01-2010 (both dates inclusive)

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Application Fee

The notification does not mention any application fee. Candidates are advised to check the official Indian Navy recruitment website www.joinindiannavy.gov.in for any fee-related information before submitting the online application.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be based on JEE (Main) 2026 CRL-based shortlisting, followed by SSB Interview, Medical Examination, and Police & Character Verification. Merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks and medical fitness. Candidates will be appointed subject to Police Verification, Character Verification, and availability of vacancies in the entry. Mere inclusion in the common merit list does not confer a vested right to appointment. Mere empanelment under no circumstances can be treated as final selection.

Stage 1 - Shortlisting Based on JEE (Main) 2026 CRL

Naval Headquarters reserves the right to fix the cut-off for shortlisting of applications for SSB based on JEE (Main) All India Common Rank List (CRL) 2026. All candidates must fill their CRL Rank in the application. Shortlisted candidates will be informed about their SSB interview schedule through email and SMS. Candidates must not change their email/mobile number until the selection process is over.

Stage 2 - Service Selection Board (SSB) Interview

SSB interviews for shortlisted candidates will be scheduled at Bengaluru / Bhopal / Kolkata / Visakhapatnam from September 2026 onwards. Change of SSB Centre is not permissible under any circumstances. Candidates must download the call-up letter on receiving intimation from Naval Headquarters via SMS/email. AC 3-tier rail fare is admissible for SSB interview if appearing for the first time for this particular type of commission — candidates must bring a photocopy of the first page of passbook or cheque leaf with Name, A/C No., and IFSC details. No compensation is admissible in case of any injury sustained during SSB tests.

Stage 3 - Medical Examination

All candidates recommended by SSB must undergo medical examination as per standards applicable to 10+2 (B.Tech) entry. No relaxation in medical standards on any grounds. Candidates already declared medically fit for NDA/INA Jan 27 need not repeat medical examination. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.

Stage 4 - Common Merit List & Appointment

Final merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks and medical fitness. Candidates will be appointed subject to Police Verification, Character Verification, and availability of vacancies. All vacancies are to be filled as per service requirement and statutory guidelines issued from time to time.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Training Details

Selected candidates will be inducted as Cadets for the four-year B.Tech Course at the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala, in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Naval Architecture & Shipbuilding (only for 07 selected candidates from Mechanical Engineering at NCW, Kochi) as per Naval requirements. On completion of the course, B.Tech Degree will be awarded by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). The entire cost of training including books and reading material will be borne by the Indian Navy. Cadets will also be provided with entitled clothing and messing. Details of pay, allowances, group insurance, gratuity, leave entitlements, and duties of officers are available on www.joinindiannavy.gov.in.

How to Apply for Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme January 2027

Candidates must register and submit their application online only at the official Indian Navy recruitment website www.joinindiannavy.gov.in. No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates are advised to read all instructions on the website carefully before submitting the online application. The application once submitted is final and no request for amendments or changes will be entertained.

  • Date of Birth proof (as per 10th/12th Class certificate)
  • 10th Class marksheet
  • 12th Class marksheet
  • JEE (Main) 2026 Score Card indicating Common Rank List (CRL)
  • Recent passport-size colour photograph

Documents to be Produced / Carried at the time of SSB Interview:

  • Print-out of the submitted online application form
  • Original certificates/documents as submitted during online application
  • Photocopy of first page of bank passbook or cheque leaf (showing Name, A/C No., and IFSC details) — for rail fare reimbursement claim

Candidates must ensure that all details including email address and mobile number are mandatory fields and are correctly filled. DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is ₹100 (One Hundred only). Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Serviceman categories are fully exempted from paying the fee. Ex-Servicemen who have already secured regular civil employment under the Central Government or Government of NCT of Delhi after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for fee exemption.

Payment must be made only through SBI ePay. No other payment mode will be accepted, and fees paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be made through a Computer Based Written Examination under one of three examination schemes depending on the post applied for.

One Tier General (I-T-G) — Post Codes 34/26, 39/26, 40/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Five sections of 40 marks each: General Awareness, General Intelligence & Reasoning Ability, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability, Hindi Language & Comprehension, and English Language & Comprehension. Final merit is based on written examination marks only.

One Tier Technical (I-T-T) — Post Codes 21/26 to 31/26, 32/26, 33/26, 35/26 to 38/26, 45/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks covering General Awareness, Reasoning, Arithmetic, Hindi, and English (20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks on the domain subject for the post concerned. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine the final merit list.

One Tier Technical/Teaching (I-T-T) — Post Codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26, 44/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks (same five general subjects, 20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks from subject-specific content including teaching methodology/B.Ed. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine final merit.

Minimum Qualifying Marks:

Ex-Servicemen 5% relaxation in respective category (minimum 30%)

Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks will be deducted for each wrong MCQ answer. Skill Test, Aptitude Test, Trade Test, or Physical Endurance Test may be conducted additionally as per job requirements. Marks will be normalized (if required) using the Score Normalisation Based on Deviation Method formula published by DSSSB vide Notice No. 10(271)/Sec.Cell/DSSSB/18/989 dated 11.07.2018.

TGT posts (Post Codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26) carry the highest pay scale at Pay Level 7 (₹44,900 – ₹1,42,400).

How to Apply

The application process for DSSSB Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. No applications sent by post, by hand, or by email will be accepted.

  1. Visit the official DSSSB registration and application portal at https://dsssbonline.nic.in.
  2. If you are a new user, complete the one-time registration process. Note down your User ID and password — the same credentials are to be used for all future DSSSB examinations; do not register multiple times.
  3. Log in using your registered credentials and select the relevant post code from Advertisement No. 03/2026.
  4. Fill in all fields of the online application form accurately. Once submitted, no change or correction — including change of category — will be permitted under any circumstances.
  5. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white or off-white background, full face, front view, eyes open) and your signature. Blurred or illegible photographs/signatures will result in rejection.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹100 through SBI ePay (exempted categories need not pay).
  7. Submit the form and take a printout for your own records. Keep the registration number and application number safely.

The application portal will be live from 16 June 2026 (12:00 Noon) until 15 July 2026 (11:59 PM), after which the link will be disabled.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Candidates applying for DSSSB 2026 should be careful about a few common pitfalls in the online application process.

Photo and signature uploads are a frequent reason for rejection — ensure the image files are clear, correctly sized, and within the file-size limit specified on the portal. Blurred or illegible uploads will cause outright rejection of candidature. If the payment gateway shows an error after fee deduction, do not immediately retry; wait for a few hours to check whether the payment was credited before attempting again through the portal's payment history section. Use an updated browser (Chrome or Firefox preferred) and avoid mobile browsers for form submission, as they may not render all fields correctly. Save your User ID and password immediately after registration and store your application number carefully — all future communications from DSSSB will reference these. Avoid applying on the last day; DSSSB expressly states it will not be responsible for inability to submit due to heavy server load near the closing date.

Bank of Baroda is hiring for 86 vacancies across 5 officer-level posts in its Corporate and Institutional Credit (C&IC) department, ranging from Manager to Chief Manager grade in both Credit Analyst and C&IC Relationship roles. Online registration opened on 16 June 2026, and the last date to apply and pay the fee is 6 July 2026. Eligible candidates need a postgraduate finance qualification or CA/CMA/CS/CFA, relevant banking credit experience, and willingness to serve anywhere in India.

Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026: Key Dates You Need to Know

This recruitment drive was announced under advertisement number BOB/HRM/REC/ADVT/2026/10. There are only two dates that matter for candidates: when the application window opens and when it closes, since the bank has not yet announced an online test date.

86 Vacancies Across 5 Posts: Full Position-wise Breakdown

The 86 vacancies are divided into two job families: Credit Analyst posts and C&IC Relationship posts, each spanning three or two seniority grades respectively. Vacancy count, age limit, and required post-qualification experience vary by grade, so candidates should check the exact post they qualify for before applying.

The educational qualification for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 is identical across all 5 posts, while the age limit and experience requirement increase with seniority.   • Age: Calculated as on 1 June 2026, ranging from a minimum of 25 years (Manager grade) to a maximum of 42 years (Chief Manager grade).
  • Nationality: Indian citizens are eligible, along with certain categories of Nepali, Bhutanese, Tibetan refugee, and Indian-origin candidates from specified countries, subject to an eligibility certificate from the Government of India where applicable.
  • Posting Condition: Only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, since the bank can post selected officers to any branch or office at its discretion.

OBC candidates falling under the creamy layer, or whose caste does not appear in the Central List, are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply as General. EWS candidates must hold a valid Income and Asset Certificate, and there is no reservation for ex-servicemen in the officers' cadre for this recruitment.

Age Relaxation Rules for Reserved Categories

The age limits mentioned above apply to General category candidates as on 1 June 2026. Candidates from reserved categories get additional years added to the upper age limit, but only for posts where reservation roster points actually exist.

Pay Scale and Salary Structure for Each Grade

Pay for Bank of Baroda C&IC officers follows the standard bipartite settlement scale used across the banking industry, with the figure increasing through fixed annual increments up to a ceiling for each grade. Selected candidates also receive allowances and perquisites as per the bank's policies, in addition to this basic pay.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

CIBIL Score Requirement: A Credit History Check Unique to This Recruitment

Unlike most government recruitment notifications, this advertisement makes personal credit history a formal eligibility condition. Candidates need a minimum CIBIL score of 680 at the time of joining the bank, since this post involves handling corporate credit decisions.

Anyone who has defaulted on loan repayments or credit card dues, or who has adverse reports from CIBIL or other external credit assessment agencies, will be treated as ineligible for appointment. The bank has reserved the right to reject a candidate's selection at any stage, including after joining, if their credit profile turns out to be unsatisfactory.

Probation Period and Mandatory Service Bond

Selected candidates do not join in a permanent capacity immediately; they first complete a probation period, and they must also commit to a minimum service period backed by a financial bond.

  • Probation Period: 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • Service Bond: Candidates must serve the bank for a minimum of 3 years from the date of joining, or pay ₹5 lakh in lieu of completing the bond period.

The exact bond terms will be confirmed in each selected candidate's offer letter and are subject to revision as per the bank's prevailing policy.

Application Fee for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

The application fee for this recruitment is fixed by category and must be paid online; it is non-refundable even if the online test is not conducted or the candidate is not shortlisted for an interview.

Category Application Fee
General, EWS & OBC ₹850 (inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges
SC, ST, PWD, ESM/DESM & Women ₹175 (inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges

Selection Process: Online Test, Psychometric Assessment & Interview

Selection for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 can include application scrutiny, an online test, a psychometric assessment, a group discussion, and a personal interview, though the bank retains the right to skip or modify any stage. Final selection depends on combined performance across whichever stages are actually conducted.

Online Test Pattern (Tentative)

If a written test is held, it will be a 150-mark, 150-minute online exam split into four sections, three of which only need to be passed rather than scored well in.

Section Test Questions Marks Duration
1 Reasoning 25 25 75 minutes (combined)
2 English Language 25 25
3 Quantitative Aptitude 25 25
4 Professional Knowledge 75 150 75 minutes
Total 150 225 150 minutes

Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge will be available bilingually in English and Hindi, while the English Language section will be in English only. Sections 1 to 3 are qualifying only and do not count toward the final score; candidates need at least 40% in General/EWS or 35% in Reserved categories to clear each of these sections, and there is no negative marking anywhere in the test.

Personal Interview & Final Merit

Candidates who clear the online test (or are otherwise shortlisted) move on to a psychometric assessment and/or personal interview, where the minimum qualifying score is 60% for General category and 55% for Reserved category candidates. If two or more candidates tie at the cut-off mark, the older candidate is ranked higher in the merit list.

The online test, if conducted, is tentatively planned across more than two dozen cities, including Mumbai, Delhi/NCR, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Jaipur, Lucknow, Baroda, Bhopal, Chandigarh-Mohali, and several other regional centres, with the final allotted centre confirmed in the call letter.

Documents Required During the Recruitment Process

Candidates do not need to upload every certificate while registering online, but they must be ready to produce the following documents in original, along with self-attested photocopies, at the interview stage or whenever the bank asks for them.

  • Printout of the interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate, SSLC/Std. X marksheet, or equivalent)
  • A valid photo identity proof such as PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, or Aadhaar card (Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Year-wise/semester-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate for SC/ST/OBC candidates, with the OBC certificate carrying a valid non-creamy-layer clause
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board, for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities
  • Income and Asset Certificate, for candidates applying under the EWS category
  • Service/discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof, for ex-servicemen candidates
  • No Objection Certificate from the current employer, for candidates already working in government, quasi-government, or public sector roles
  • Documentary proof of declared work experience, such as appointment letters, salary slips, or relieving letters

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Apply Online

Bank of Baroda accepts applications for this recruitment only through its official website; no offline or postal applications will be considered.

  1. Visit www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and navigate to the Careers section, then Current Opportunities.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active until the recruitment process is complete.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and work experience details carefully, since no changes are allowed once the form is submitted.
  4. Upload your photograph (200 x 230 pixels, 20-50 KB) and signature (140 x 60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, signed in your normal handwriting and not in capital letters.
  5. Upload your resume, Date of Birth proof, educational certificates (combined in one PDF), and category/PWD/experience certificates where applicable, each as a PDF on A4 size not exceeding 500 KB.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  7. Save and print the system-generated application form and fee receipt for your future reference.

Apply Online for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

Job Profile: What Will You Actually Do in This Role?

The two job families under this recruitment involve noticeably different day-to-day work, which is worth understanding before choosing which post to apply for.

Credit Analyst roles (Manager/Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are appraisal-focused: examining new and existing corporate credit proposals, conducting credit due-diligence on financial, industry, and business risk, coordinating with Relationship Managers, and ensuring compliance in corporate accounts.

C&IC Relationship roles (Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are client-facing: maintaining relationships with existing corporate clients, sourcing new-to-bank corporate borrowers, cross-selling ancillary business, and creating account plans with opportunity income analysis for corporate borrowers.

Mistakes That Could Cost You This Opportunity

Several avoidable errors can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate from Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026, so it helps to check these before hitting submit.

  • Assuming any postgraduate degree qualifies - only a finance-specialised PG degree/diploma or a CA/CMA/CS/CFA qualification meets the educational criteria.
  • Not checking your CIBIL score in advance - a score below 680, or any default history, can lead to rejection even after selection.
  • Counting clerical-cadre banking experience toward the eligibility criteria, which is explicitly excluded.
  • Including work experience of less than 6 months from a previous organisation, which will not be counted unless it is part of your current employment.
  • Submitting more than one application - only the latest valid one is retained, and fees paid for earlier ones are forfeited.
  • Selecting a category casually, since no change of category is allowed after registration and an invalid OBC/EWS claim without supporting certificates can affect your candidature.
  • Overlooking the 3-year/₹5 lakh service bond commitment before deciding whether to accept the role if selected.
  • Waiting until the last date to register, risking last-minute website load issues for which the bank takes no responsibility.

Here is a government-linked job opportunity that most people overlook simply because it does not come with flashy headlines. CSC e-Governance Services India Limited, the agency that powers Digital India's grassroots service delivery, is actively recruiting Aadhaar Supervisors and Operators for Aadhaar Seva Kendras (ASKs) across five states - and the educational bar is as accessible as it gets.

If you have passed Class 12, hold a UIDAI-authorized Aadhaar Operator or Supervisor certification, and have basic computer skills, you are eligible. The position is offered on a 1-year contract basis with remuneration pegged to the minimum wages for semi-skilled manpower in your respective state.

Vacancies are open across Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Tripura, with specific district-level slots available. The last date to apply is July 20, 2026.

Apply Now at https://career.csccloud.in

What Is an Aadhaar Seva Kendra and Why Does This Role Matter?

Before jumping to the eligibility details, it helps to understand what you are actually applying for. Aadhaar Seva Kendras (ASKs) are dedicated centers set up by UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) across the country where residents can enroll for Aadhaar, update their biometric and demographic information, and avail other Aadhaar-related services.

CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd, a Special Purpose Vehicle under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), operates many of these centers as part of its Digital India mandate. The Aadhaar Supervisor oversees the operations at the ASK and manages operators, while the Aadhaar Operator directly handles resident-facing Aadhaar enrolment and update tasks under UIDAI guidelines.

This is a frontline government service delivery role - one that directly impacts how millions of Indians access identity-linked benefits and services.

Who Is Eligible to Apply? Full Eligibility Criteria Explained

The eligibility requirements for this CSC recruitment are deliberately inclusive, targeting candidates from smaller towns and districts who are already part of the Digital India ecosystem. Here is every condition you need to satisfy.

Age Requirement

Candidates must be a minimum of 18 years of age. There is no upper age limit specified in the notification, making this position accessible to a wider demographic including older candidates seeking re-employment.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must meet one of the following educational qualifications:

Option 1 – Class 12 Pass Intermediate / Senior Secondary certificate from a recognized board.

Option 2 – Matriculation + ITI Class 10 (Matriculation) pass followed by a 2-year Industrial Training Institute (ITI) certificate in any trade.

Option 3 – Matriculation + Polytechnic Diploma Class 10 (Matriculation) pass followed by a 3-year Polytechnic Diploma from a recognized institution.

Mandatory Certification – UIDAI Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor Certificate

This is the most critical eligibility condition and the one most candidates miss. You must hold a valid Aadhaar Operator or Supervisor Certificate issued by a Testing & Certifying Agency authorized by UIDAI for delivering Aadhaar services.

There are two ways to obtain this certification:

Path 1 – Aadhaar Supervisor Exam: You can take the Aadhaar Supervisor exam through the UIDAI exam portal. When you apply, an authorization request is sent to the State Team. After their approval, you can appear for the exam at: https://uidai.dexitglobalexams.com/UIDAI/LoginAction.action

Path 2 – Aadhaar LMS Certification: Once your LMS (Learning Management System) ID and password are created and approved, you can appear for the LMS Certification through: https://e-learning.uidai.gov.in

Basic Computer Skills

Candidates must have foundational computer proficiency. This is essential given that all Aadhaar enrolment and update operations are conducted on dedicated UIDAI software.

Who Cannot Apply

VLEs (Village Level Entrepreneurs) are explicitly not eligible to apply for this position. This exclusion is clearly stated in all the CSC job postings for this recruitment.

Remuneration: What Will You Earn?

The salary for CSC Aadhaar Supervisor/Operator positions is benchmarked against the minimum wages for semi-skilled manpower as notified by the respective state government. This means the actual take-home pay will vary depending on the state where you are posted.

Since each state government periodically revises minimum wage notifications, candidates should check the current semi-skilled minimum wage applicable in their state to understand the exact compensation they can expect. The contract is for 1 year, after which renewal would depend on organizational requirements.

Contract Terms: What to Expect Before You Join

This is a purely contractual engagement for a period of 1 (one) year only. Understanding the nature of this role before applying helps avoid disappointment later.

  • The engagement is with CSC e-Governance Services India Limited, not directly with UIDAI or the Government of India
  • You will be deployed at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) in your assigned district
  • The role involves direct interaction with residents seeking Aadhaar enrolment, biometric updates, and demographic corrections
  • Working under this contract does not automatically lead to regularization or a permanent government job
  • VLEs who are already operating CSC Common Service Centers are ineligible to apply, as these are separate operational roles

How to Apply for CSC Aadhaar Supervisor/Operator 2026

The entire application process is handled through the CSC Career Portal. Here is how to apply step by step.

Step 1: Visit the official CSC career portal at https://career.csccloud.in

Step 2: Browse the active job listings and identify the specific posting for your state and district. Note that Madhya Pradesh has two separate listings - check both to find your district.

Step 3: Click the "Apply Now" button on the relevant job posting page.

Step 4: Complete the application form with your personal, educational, and certification details. Keep your UIDAI Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate details ready for upload.

Step 5: Submit your application before the deadline.

Don't Have the UIDAI Certificate Yet? Here's What to Do Right Now

If you meet the educational and age eligibility but haven't yet obtained the mandatory UIDAI Aadhaar Operator or Supervisor certificate, you still have time before July 20, 2026 - but you need to act immediately.

Step 1 – Register for the Exam:
Visit https://uidai.dexitglobalexams.com/UIDAI/LoginAction.action and register for the Aadhaar Supervisor examination.

Step 2 – Get State Team Authorization:
After you apply for the exam, an authorization request goes to the State Team. They must approve it before you can sit the exam. This can take a few days, so apply without delay.

Step 3 – Alternatively, Try LMS Certification:
If you already have an LMS ID and password, log in at https://e-learning.uidai.gov.in to attempt the LMS-based certification route.

Step 4 – Download Your Certificate:
Once you pass the exam, download your UIDAI-authorized certificate and keep it ready to submit with your CSC application.

Time is limited. The certification process involves state-level authorization that adds waiting time. Start today if you want to apply before July 20, 2026.
