Experience Requirements

  • Associate Engineer Grade II: Minimum 5 years of post-qualification relevant experience
  • Associate Engineer Grade III: Minimum 9 years of post-qualification relevant experience
  • The cut-off date for experience calculation is 31 May 2026

Age Limit

  • Associate Engineer Grade II: Maximum 37 years as on 31 May 2026
  • Associate Engineer Grade III: Maximum 41 years as on 31 May 2026

Age Relaxation and Concessions

EIL provides age relaxation for several reserved and special categories in line with Government of India directives. This ensures that eligible candidates from diverse backgrounds have a fair opportunity to apply.

Category Age Relaxation
SC / ST 5 years
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
Persons with Disability (PwD) – General / EWS 10 years
PwD – OBC (NCL) 13 years
PwD – SC / ST 15 years
Ex-Servicemen As per GoI rules

PwD Note: Only persons with 40% or more disability are eligible to apply under the PwD category.

Salary and Remuneration for EIL Fixed Term Engineers 2026

One of the most attractive aspects of this EIL recruitment is the competitive consolidated monthly remuneration, which varies by city category and grade. The pay package includes HRA and PF components.

Designation X Category Cities Y Category Cities Z Category Cities
Associate Engineer Grade II ₹80,000/month ₹76,000/month ₹72,000/month
Associate Engineer Grade III ₹96,000/month ₹91,200/month ₹86,400/month

Additional Benefits

Beyond the monthly consolidated pay, EIL also provides a set of value-added benefits to all fixed term engineers:

  • Medical Insurance: Reimbursement of Medical Insurance Premium for self, up to ₹2,00,000 per annum
  • Out-of-Pocket Expenses: Reimbursement for working beyond standard working hours
  • GPAI Scheme: Coverage under the Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme as per Company Policy
  • Travelling Allowance: Payment for official travel outside the place of posting
  • Paid Leave: 2 days of paid leave for each completed month of service

Terms and Conditions of EIL Fixed Term Employment

Before applying, candidates must be aware of the contractual nature of this engagement. EIL's fixed term employment comes with specific conditions that differ from permanent PSU roles.

  • The engagement is purely on a fixed term basis, initially for 2 years, extendable up to a maximum of 3 years from the date of joining, subject to satisfactory performance
  • The engagement will automatically terminate on the expiry of the term unless extended
  • Candidates may be required to work anywhere in India and abroad
  • Only medically fit candidates will be permitted to join
  • No claim for regular/permanent appointment in EIL shall be entertained on the basis of fixed term service
  • Selected candidates must join within 15 days of the announcement of results

Place of Posting

The primary place of posting for all selected candidates will be in the National Capital Region (NCR). However, EIL may deploy engineers anywhere in India or abroad based on project and organizational requirements. Candidates must be prepared for transfers and outstation postings as a condition of this role.

Walk-in Interview Schedule, Venue, and Cities

The walk-in interview for EIL Recruitment 2026 is scheduled across major cities in India, providing candidates from various regions a convenient opportunity to appear. This section covers the tentative timeline and the cities where interviews will be held.

  • Tentative Interview Start Date: 13 July 2026
  • Exact Date: Will be communicated separately via the candidate's registered email ID
  • Interview Cities: Gurugram, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, and Vadodara
  • Interview Timing: Interviews may be held up to 8:00 PM on the same day and, if required, continued the next day. Candidates must make their own arrangements for accommodation.

Candidates based in Chennai will have the option to attend their interview locally, making this a convenient opportunity for Tamil Nadu-based engineers.

Documents Required for the Walk-in Interview

Candidates must carry all required documents in original along with one set of self-attested photocopies. Missing any document may result in disqualification.

Mandatory Documents

  1. 6 copies of the duly filled and submitted online application form with a recent colour photograph affixed
  2. Photo Identity Proof (any one): Driving License / PAN Card / Passport / Voter ID / Aadhar Card
  3. Date of Birth Proof: Matriculation / Class X Certificate / Birth Certificate
  4. Educational Certificates: Mark sheets and passing certificates for Class X, HSC, Degree, and Post Graduation (all semesters/years)
  5. CGPA Conversion Proof from the University/Institute (if applicable)
  6. Experience Certificates (originals) for all experiences mentioned in the application, clearly showing dates of joining and separation, and nature of work
  7. Additional employment proof on demand: Offer letter, confirmation order, pay slips, PF statement, ESI Card, Bank Statement

Category-Specific Documents (if applicable)

  • SC/ST Certificate (in prescribed format from competent authority)
  • Valid OBC (NCL) Certificate (in GoI prescribed format)
  • Valid EWS Certificate
  • Disability Certificate
  • Discharge Certificate and relevant proforma for Ex-Servicemen
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) if currently employed in a Central/State Government or Autonomous Body

Important: If any original document is unavailable on the day of the interview, the candidate will not be considered for further selection.

How to Apply Online for EIL Walk-in Interview 2026

The application process for EIL Recruitment 2026 is entirely online through the official EIL website. Here is the complete step-by-step guide to apply without errors.

Step 1: Visit the official EIL website career section at http://www.engineersindia.com

Step 2: Read all the instructions on the website carefully before beginning the registration

Step 3: Fill in the online form with all accurate details. Round off your percentage to the lower whole number (e.g., 60.9 → 60) and CGPA to the lower decimal (e.g., 6.95 → 6.9)

Step 4: Keep the following scanned documents ready before you begin:

  • Passport-size colour photograph in .jpg/.jpeg format (max 75 KB)
  • Signature in .jpg/.jpeg format (max 25 KB)

Step 5: After submitting the form online, take 6 printouts of the application form, affix a colour photograph on each, and bring them to the walk-in interview

Step 6: Confirm that all details are correct - the cut-off date for experience and age is 31 May 2026

[Apply Online] – Visit https://recruitment.eil.co.in/ between 00:00 hrs on 16 June 2026 and 23:59 hrs on 30 June 2026

[PDF Download Link] – Download the official EIL Recruitment Notification HRD/Rectt./Advt./2026-27/05 from the EIL careers page for complete details.

Important Dates for EIL Recruitment 2026

Staying on top of key deadlines is essential to ensure you don't miss out on this opportunity.

Event Date
Online Application Opens 16 June 2026 (00:00 hrs)
Online Application Closes 30 June 2026 (23:59 hrs)
Eligibility Cut-off Date 31 May 2026
Walk-in Interview (Tentative) From 13 July 2026
Exact Interview Date Communication Via registered email

Important Instructions for Applicants

Before you finalize your application, go through these critical instructions issued by EIL to avoid rejection:

  • Only candidates who meet all eligibility criteria should apply
  • Candidates wishing to apply for multiple positions must submit separate online applications for each post
  • Your registered email address must remain valid for at least 24 months from the date of application submission, as all correspondence (including interview intimation) will be sent via email
  • Any updates, corrigenda, or clarifications will be published only on www.engineersindia.com - no separate press notifications will be issued
  • Providing wrong or false information will lead to immediate disqualification
  • No travel or stay allowances will be paid by EIL for attending the interview
  • Any legal disputes will be subject to the jurisdiction of courts in Delhi
  • EIL reserves the right to cancel the advertisement or the selection process without assigning any reason

Disclaimer: This article is based solely on the official Engineers India Limited recruitment advertisement (HRD/Rectt./Advt./2026-27/05). Candidates are advised to visit the official EIL website www.engineersindia.com for the latest updates, corrigenda, or changes to the notification.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs

Eligibility for forest department jobs depends on the post, state and recruitment authority. Below is a general idea of qualification and age for popular posts like Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer. Candidates should always check the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Forest Guard / Field Guard / Forest Watcher / Beat Guard: Usually 10th pass or 12th pass from a recognized board, knowledge of local language, and basic physical standards as per state rules.
  • Forester / Section Forest Officer / Deputy Forest Ranger: Generally 12th pass or graduate in any stream or science-related subjects, with physical standards and sometimes driving or technical skills depending on the post.
  • Forest Range Officer (RFO) / Forest Ranger / ACF: Normally graduate degree in Science, Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Science, Engineering or related disciplines, with higher physical standards and sometimes a competitive exam similar to state PCS level.
  • IFS / Indian Forest Service and senior posts (DCF, CF, CCF, PCCF): Filled through UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination and promotions, requiring a graduate degree and all-India competitive selection.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • Forest Guard / Forester / Field Guard: Minimum age is usually 18 years and maximum age is around 27–30 years, with age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Ex-servicemen and other categories as per government rules.
  • Forest Range Officer / ACF and higher competitive posts: Age limit often ranges from 21 to 32 years (varies by recruitment), with relaxations for reserved categories.
  • Exact age limit, cut-off date and relaxation details always depend on the particular notification, so candidates should verify from the official advertisement before applying.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The selection process for Forest Department Jobs 2026 typically includes written examinations, physical tests and document verification. Some posts also conduct medical examination and walking tests due to the demanding nature of field duties.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  • Written Exam: Most Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer recruitments start with a written exam based on objective-type questions (MCQs).
  • PET / PST (Physical Efficiency Test / Physical Standard Test): Candidates who qualify written exam are called for running, walking test, height, chest measurement and other physical parameters as per post and gender.
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates of age, qualification, caste, residence, sports/NCC and other documents mentioned in the notification.
  • Medical Examination: Many forest posts require medical fitness to ensure candidates can perform field duties in forests, wildlife areas and difficult terrain.

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

Typical syllabus for written exam may include:

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs (national, state-level, environment and forest-related topics)
  • General Hindi / English or regional language (grammar, comprehension, vocabulary)
  • General Mathematics / Quantitative Aptitude (up to 10th or 12th level)
  • General Science and Environmental Studies (forest, wildlife, biodiversity, conservation, climate, basic biology)
  • Reasoning Ability (logical and analytical reasoning)

Exact subject-wise marks, number of questions, negative marking and exam duration will be given in the respective forest department notification.

  2. Find the latest link for Forest Guard / Forester / Forest Range Officer / other forest posts and open the detailed advertisement.
  3. Complete the registration process with basic details like name, mobile number, email ID and verify using OTP if required.
  4. Fill the online application form with personal, educational, address and category information exactly as per documents.
  5. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature and other certificates in the prescribed format and size.
  6. Pay the application fee online through Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card or UPI as per your convenience.
  7. Finally, submit the form and take a printout or PDF of the submitted application and payment receipt for future reference.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has released Advertisement No. 06/2026 inviting Online Recruitment Applications for 538 posts across more than 30 central government ministries and departments. Posts span disciplines including civil aviation, defence, forensic science, agriculture, mines, law, and education. Applications must be submitted through the UPSC ORA portal at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Age Relaxation

The standard age relaxations applicable to these posts are as follows. SC candidates receive 5 additional years, OBC candidates receive 3 additional years, and all PwBD candidates receive 10 additional years over and above their category relaxation. For certain posts with a base upper limit of 50 years, the PwBD maximum is capped at 56 years - this applies to the Regional Director (NCONF), Professor Sugar Engineering (NSI), Principal (A&N), and Consultant Ophthalmologist (UT Ladakh). UPSC may relax qualifications and experience at its discretion in writing for candidates otherwise well qualified.

Grade Point to Percentage Conversion (CME Pune and UT Ladakh posts)

Where a grade point system is in use and no conversion formula has been notified by the institution, the following equivalences apply as stated in the notification:

CGPA Equivalent Percentage
6.25 55%
6.75 60%
7.25 65%
7.75 70%
8.25 75%

For UT Ladakh Lecturer and Engineering posts, ST candidates receive a 5% relaxation at Bachelor's and Master's level, making 55% (or equivalent grade) the minimum eligibility.

Special Condition - UT Ladakh Posts (Posts 60-70)

All posts under the Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh are exclusively open to Domiciles of UT Ladakh. A valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Tehsildar under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment Rules, 2025 (published in the Gazette of India on 03.06.2025) is mandatory. Two eligible categories exist: Category A (holders of or eligible for Ladakh Resident Certificate) and Category B (children of LRC holders or those eligible). Reservation is governed by the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004, as extended to UT Ladakh and amended by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 (No. 1 of 2025), and further by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Rules, 2025 notified vide S.O. 77 dated 27.06.2025.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

UPSC is conducting this recruitment by selection. The notification does not describe specific stages such as written examination or interview. The selection method will be as determined by UPSC for each post individually. No exam dates or result timelines are stated in the source.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes

Candidates applying through the UPSC ORA portal can avoid common problems by following these general practices. Photograph and signature files must meet the portal's specified size and dimension requirements; uploading files that are too large or in an unsupported format is among the most frequent causes of incomplete applications. If a payment transaction fails, wait for the system to confirm the failure before attempting to pay again - making duplicate payments can cause complications that require manual resolution. Use an updated, stable browser on a desktop or laptop for the best experience; mobile browsers sometimes fail to render form fields correctly. Save your registration number and password immediately after registering, as the portal requires them for every subsequent login. Do not attempt to submit your application on the final day of the application window, as heavy traffic on the server is common and can cause timeouts or session errors.

SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 - Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The examination consists of two parts: Part-I (Computer Based & Written Examination, 300 marks) and Part-II (Evaluation of Record of Service/APARs, 100 marks). Total marks = 400. Note: There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in Computer Based Examination (Paper-I). Paper Subject Syllabus / Topics
Paper-I (CBE) General Awareness Questions aimed at testing General Awareness of the environment around and its application to society. Paper-I (CBE) English Language and Comprehension Understanding and knowledge of English language: Vocabulary, spelling, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, sentence completion, phrases and idiomatic use of words, comprehension of a passage. Questions will be of matriculation level.

Mode of Selection

Step 1 Based on performance in Paper-I (CBE) of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of Paper-II (Descriptive Paper) of Part-I. Candidates not qualifying Paper-I will not be evaluated for Paper-II and will not be considered for further selection.
Step 2 Based on aggregate performance in Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of record of service (Part-II). Candidates not qualifying Part-I aggregate will not be eligible for Part-II evaluation.

How to Apply for SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025

The process has two parts - One Time Registration (OTR) followed by the application - plus a mandatory offline forwarding step. Follow these steps:

  1. Generate OTR on the new website. Visit ssc.gov.in and click "Register Now." Any OTR created on the old site (ssc.nic.in) will not work on the new portal.

  4. Fill the application - service details, cadre, crucial date, length of service, and age-relaxation code (if any). Information auto-filled from OTR is non-editable; use "Modify Registration" if a correction is needed.
  5. Capture your live photograph and upload your signature as per the specifications (see below).
  6. Upload the required documents (listed below) and Submit. Take a printout of the submitted application.
  7. Forward the hard copy through proper channel. Your Head of Department / Head of Office must forward the printed application along with service documents to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 03-07-2026 (6:00 PM) - or 10-07-2026 for candidates abroad/A&N/Lakshadweep.

Critical: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Office will be admitted. A correctly submitted online form alone is not enough.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Start

  • Certified true copy of the first page of your Service Book (attested by HoD/HoO)
  • Certified particulars of service (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment)
  • Class 12th certificate / educational qualification proof (if applicable)
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST), if claiming reservation
  • Disability certificate (Annexure-VII / VIII) for PwBD candidates
  • A recent passport-size photo for the live capture reference, and a scanned signature

Photograph & Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: Captured live via webcam/phone, in a well-lit area with a plain background. No cap, mask, or spectacles. Face must fill the on-screen red rectangle. Pre-existing/scanned photos are rejected.
  • Signature: JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, dimensions about 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm. Sign so the signature fills at least 80% of the box. Blurred or miniature signatures are rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Exam Pattern & Scheme

The examination carries 260 marks in total - 200 for Part-I (the exams) and 60 for Part-II (service record). Note that Paper-I is descriptive (written) and Paper-II is the objective Computer Based Test (CBT).

Part-I: Written + Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Paper Type Section Questions Max Marks Duration
Paper-I Descriptive (Written) Short Essay – 100 1 hr 30 min*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (a) Language - General English or Samanya Hindi 50 50 2 hrs*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (b) General Knowledge 50 50 (combined)

*Scribe-eligible candidates get 2 hours for Paper-I and 2 hours 40 minutes for Paper-II, plus 20 minutes compensatory time per hour.

  • Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applies to Paper-II (CBT) only. There is no negative marking in the descriptive Paper-I.
  • Candidates must attempt the exam in the language (English/Hindi) chosen in the application form.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (60 Marks)

60 marks are reserved for evaluation of the APARs (Annual Performance Appraisal Reports). These marks are added to determine the final rank. Once evaluated, no request to change APAR grading is entertained.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Selection Process

This is a competitive, not qualifying examination. Selection proceeds stage by stage:

  1. Paper-II (CBT) qualifying: Candidates must clear the minimum marks fixed for Paper-II to have their Paper-I evaluated.
  2. Paper-I (Descriptive) evaluation: Only those qualifying in Paper-II have their descriptive paper assessed.
  3. APAR evaluation (Part-II): Based on the aggregate of Paper-I + Paper-II, shortlisted candidates move to service-record evaluation.
  4. Final merit: Prepared on the combined total of Paper-I + Paper-II + Part-II (APAR) = 260 marks, cadre-wise, subject to reservation. Ties are resolved by Paper-I marks, then Paper-II part (a), then Paper-II total, then date of birth (older ranked higher), then alphabetical order.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Syllabus

  • Paper-I (Short Essay): One essay of 400–500 words on any of the specified subjects.
  • Paper-II (a) Language: Simple composition and applied grammar (in the chosen English/Hindi medium).
  • Paper-II (b) General Knowledge: Current events, matters of everyday observation and experience, and general information about India.

SSC JSA / LDC Salary 2026

Selected candidates are appointed in Pay Level-2 (₹19,900 – ₹63,200 per month) under the 7th CPC, as Group 'C' Non-Gazetted staff. In addition to basic pay, employees are entitled to Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and other benefits as admissible under Central Government rules for the respective department.

Common Reasons SSC Applications Get Rejected

A large share of LDCE applications fail on avoidable mistakes. Double-check all of these before submitting:

  • Application not forwarded by the Head of Department/Office (the single biggest cause of rejection).
  • Multiple applications submitted for the same exam.
  • Photograph with a cap/spectacles, dark background, blurred, or a pre-existing (scanned) photo instead of a live capture.
  • Signature that is blurred, miniature, or below the size norm.
  • Wrong OTR details - name, father's/mother's name, or date of birth not matching the matriculation certificate (OTR data is non-editable).
  • Hard copy reaching SSC-NR after the deadline, or incomplete documents.

What to Do If the SSC Website Is Slow

Traffic on the SSC portal spikes near the closing date. If you face issues:

  • Apply during off-peak hours - late at night or early morning - rather than on the last day.
  • Clear your browser cache/cookies, or use an incognito/private tab.
  • Try a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
  • Keep all documents pre-scanned and ready in the correct format so a session timeout doesn't cost you the whole form.
  • Save a draft frequently and take a printout immediately after final submission.

Exam Day Guidelines

  • The exam is conducted in Delhi-NCR only; there is no centre abroad. A candidate posted abroad must appear in India at their own expense.
  • The Admission Certificate is issued online via sscnr.nic.in (3–4 days before the exam); it is never sent by post.
  • Carry your original Departmental Identity Card along with a hard copy of the Admission Certificate.
  • Candidates not Aadhaar-authenticated during OTR must report early with two passport-size photographs and an original photo ID showing date of birth.
  • No Travelling Allowance is paid by SSC.
  • Mobile phones, Bluetooth/wireless devices, smartwatches, and electronic gadgets are strictly prohibited. SSC conducts post-exam log, biometric, and CCTV analysis, and malpractice attracts debarment of 1 to 7 years depending on the offence.

Helpline & Official Links

  • Help Desk (SSC-HQ): 1800-309-3063 (Toll-free)
  • SSC (Northern Region): 011-24363343
  • Official Websites: ssc.gov.in (HQ) · sscnr.nic.in (Northern Region)

Competition Level Analysis for Exim Bank Management Trainee Recruitment 2026

The competition level for Exim Bank MT Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very intense given that only 05 vacancies are on offer across two disciplines from a large pool of MBA/PGDBM graduates across India. The Bank being a premier financial institution under the Government of India makes this an exceptionally sought-after position among finance, HR, and administration postgraduates. The subjective Written Test format — unlike the MCQ-based bank exams — demands strong subject knowledge, analytical writing ability, and command over HR / Administration concepts rather than just speed and aptitude.

The low vacancy count means even marginal differences in written test scores will determine shortlisting for the interview round. Candidates with domain depth in HRM/Personnel Management (for MT-HRM) or Hotel/Facilities/Civil background with MBA (for MT-Administration) are better positioned. The Personal Interview carrying 30% of the final weightage means soft skills, subject clarity, and awareness of Exim Bank's functions and India's international trade ecosystem will be critical differentiators at the final stage.

Who should NOT apply for Exim Bank Management Trainee Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates who have completed their graduation or postgraduation through correspondence / part-time / open university / open learning / external / distance learning; they are categorically not eligible.
  • Candidates who do not hold a Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) in the relevant specialization with minimum 60% marks in both graduation and post graduation.
  • Candidates outside the age band of 21-28 years as on 30-04-2026 (except as per OBC/PwBD/Ex-Servicemen relaxation).
  • OBC candidates belonging to the Creamy Layer; they must apply as General candidates. OBC certificate must be valid as on the last date of applying (issued within one year prior to the last date).
  • Candidates who have defaulted in any loan repayment and/or whose name appears in CIBIL database as a defaulter.
  • Candidates unwilling to serve anywhere in India or unwilling to be transferred to offices outside India (with consent).
  • Candidates unwilling to execute a personal bond of Rs. 3 lakh to serve the Bank for 1 year as MT and minimum 5 years as employee after absorption.
  • Currently serving employees of Government / PSU who cannot produce a proper Relieving Letter/Discharge Certificate from their present employer at the time of joining.
  • Candidates whose CGPA-based qualification does not include an equivalent percentage conversion letter from the Head of Institute/Controller of Examination (if percentage is not mentioned in marksheet).

Common mistakes / What to check before applying Exim Bank Management Trainee Recruitment 2026?

  • Applying for MT-HRM without specialization in Human Resource Management / Personnel Management, or applying for MT-Administration without the prescribed qualification combinations.
  • Not checking whether your graduation and postgraduation are from a full-time regular programme; part-time/distance mode graduates are not eligible even if the university is recognized.
  • Entering less than 60% marks in either graduation or postgraduation; both must independently meet the 60% threshold.
  • OBC candidates applying with an expired caste certificate; OBC NCL certificate must be issued within one year prior to the last date of applying and must contain the non-creamy layer clause.
  • Uploading blurred/incorrect photo, signature, left thumb impression, or handwritten declaration; any mismatch or unclear document can lead to rejection.
  • Writing the handwritten declaration in capital letters or in a language other than English; both will render the application invalid.
  • Using an inactive or incorrect mobile number/email ID, causing missed notifications for call letters, exam updates, or interview communication.
  • Pressing the BACK or REFRESH button during the online payment process, which may result in double charge or payment failure.
  • Not noting down the Provisional Registration Number and Password generated at the time of registration; required for re-login if application is saved midway.
  • Submitting application without verifying that the name as filled in the form exactly matches the name on photo identity proof; any mismatch will lead to disqualification at the exam/interview stage.

How to Apply for Exim Bank Management Trainee Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online only from 15 May 2026 to 21 June 2026 through the link available at https://www.eximbankindia.in/careers. No other mode of application will be accepted. Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date and not wait till the last date.   • Signature with black ink on white paper (140×60 pixels; 10 KB-20 KB; JPEG) — not in CAPITAL LETTERS

National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) has released vacancy notices for 175 posts across two grades - Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller (34 posts, Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026) and Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager (175 posts, Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026) - on absorption basis from Regular/Contractual employees of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, and RRTS. These roles support India's first high-speed rail corridor between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. Eligibility criteria are reckoned as on 31 May 2026. Candidates must check the official NHSRCL website for the application portal link and closing date.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Quick Summary

This recruitment covers two distinct pay grades under IDA scales. The Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller grade carries the NE-6 IDA pay scale of ₹46,000–1,45,000, while the Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager grade carries the NE-4 IDA pay scale of ₹40,000–1,25,000. Both grades are open exclusively to serving employees of Indian Railways/Government Railways/Metro Railways/RRTS - this is not an open-market recruitment.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is assessed differently depending on whether the candidate is employed under IDA or CDA pay scales. All experience and eligibility conditions are reckoned as on 31 May 2026. Experience gained through teaching, faculty, apprenticeship, internship, proprietorship, partnership, or freelancing will not count toward the required years of experience.

Work Experience – Deputy Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026)

For IDA pay scale employees (Metro Railways/RRTS):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field (Civil/Track maintenance, Electrical Power Distribution, Railway Signalling, Rolling Stock maintenance, or OCC Operations as applicable); AND
  • Currently working in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹46,000, OR
  • 2 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹40,000 and above, OR
  • 5 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹37,000 and above.

For CDA pay scale employees (Ministry of Railways / other Govt. Railways):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field; AND
  • Working in PB-2 + GP ₹4,200 (Level 6 of 7th CPC); AND
  • Minimum 4 years of Group C service.

For the Deputy Chief Controller (Operations) post specifically, candidates under CDA scales must have 5 years' supervisory experience in maintenance of Rolling Stock and Depot Machinery (not OCC operations) to be eligible. Under IDA scales, the requirement is 5 years' post-qualification supervisory experience in OCC/Station/Train operations with minimum 2 years as Traffic Controller in an OCC equipped with modern OCC systems.

Note on MACP: For CDA-scale employees, higher grade pays granted under MACP by the department will not be considered for eligibility. Only the substantive grade is taken into account for determining the grade of absorption.

Work Experience – Junior Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026)

All posts require a minimum of 3 years of post-qualification experience in the relevant field within Operations & Maintenance departments of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, or RRTS systems.

The maximum age limit is 45 years for all posts in both groups. Age is reckoned as on 31 May 2026.

The application fee structure is identical for both vacancy notice groups. Female candidates and candidates from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe backgrounds are fully exempt from paying the fee. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances - candidates are advised to confirm their eligibility before making payment.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

For the Deputy Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026), selection consists of four stages in this order: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, Interview, and Medical Examination.

For the Junior Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026), selection consists of three stages: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, and Medical Examination. Note that the Interview stage is not part of the JE-grade selection process.

In both cases, management reserves the right to include or dispense with any stage of the selection methodology. Shortlisted candidates will be informed through their registered email addresses. Out-station candidates called for interview (DE grade) will be paid Travelling Allowance as per company rules.

Medical fitness is a mandatory condition of appointment. Candidates will be examined as per the Indian Railway Medical Manual (IRMM). Additional medical tests such as Audiometry and Perimetry may also be conducted as required for safe operation of High Speed Trains.

Surety Bond and Service Commitment

Candidates selected for absorption must be aware of the following binding commitments before joining NHSRCL.

Surety Bond on Joining: Selected candidates must execute a surety bond of ₹3,00,000/- committing to serve NHSRCL for a minimum period of 4 years (excluding any period on Leave Without Pay or Extra-Ordinary Leave). A prior notice of 90 days is required before resigning from the corporation.

Surety Bond on Training: If training is provided, candidates must execute a separate surety bond for the cost of training plus applicable service tax, committing to serve for a minimum of 6 years after training completion. A three-month prior notice is required before resignation in such cases.

Candidates appointed on absorption basis will be on probation for one year. They may be posted anywhere across NHSRCL offices and the MAHSR Project.

Important Note on Controller and Safety Assignment

Candidates applying for posts that include a Controller or Safety assignment (such as Vacancy Nos. 21–29, 31/2026) must indicate their willingness for such assignments in the online application form. They must also furnish their order of preference between the available designations at the time of application. However, the final allocation of post or assignment rests entirely at NHSRCL's discretion, regardless of the candidate's stated preference.

Document Requirements

Along with the application, candidates must submit a Competency Certificate or Experience Certificate issued by their employer. This certificate must clearly indicate the required work experience with year-wise details of the nature and type of work performed. Incomplete applications or applications submitted without supporting documents will be rejected outright.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Applying for NHSRCL absorption posts is a specialized process. Keep the following in mind to avoid rejection:

  • Do not apply for more than one post within the same vacancy notice group (21–25 or 26–32). Only one application is permitted per group, and both CBT sessions may be held simultaneously.
  • Save your registration credentials immediately after creating your portal account. NHSRCL communicates exclusively through registered email IDs - check your spam folder regularly.
  • Verify eligibility before paying the fee. The ₹400 fee is non-refundable under all circumstances, including ineligibility or withdrawal.
  • If your internet connection drops during payment, do not immediately retry - check your bank statement first to avoid a double payment. Contact your bank if the amount is debited but confirmation is not received.
  • Use an updated browser on a stable connection for the application portal. Avoid submitting on the final day to prevent server congestion issues.
  • Ensure your experience certificate is on your employer's letterhead with year-wise work details - general appointment letters or offer letters alone are not acceptable.

The Karnataka State Police (KSP) has officially released the KSP Recruitment 2026 notification, announcing 3,991 vacancies for the post of Civil Police Constable across two separate cadres. This is one of the biggest police recruitment drives in Karnataka in recent years, and online applications are now open on the KEA portal from 8th June 2026 to 3rd July 2026. The written examination is scheduled for 2nd August 2026.

If you are a Karnataka resident who has passed Class 12 (PUC) and has been looking for a stable government job in law enforcement, this is your chance. Read on for a complete breakdown of the KSP Constable Recruitment 2026 - from eligibility and vacancies to how to apply and what to expect in the selection process.

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

Karnataka State Police, Central Recruitment & Promotion Department, Bengaluru has officially released two notifications - Advertisement No. 01/Recruitment-4/2026-27 (Kalyana Karnataka / 371(J) cadre) and Advertisement No. 02/Recruitment-4/2026-27 (Mikkili/Okkalida cadre) - both dated 05.06.2026, for direct recruitment of Police Constable (Civil) posts. The notifications include complete details on vacancies, eligibility, selection process, exam pattern, physical standards, age relaxations, reservation, and application instructions. Candidates are strongly advised to read the full notifications before applying.

KSP Constable Eligibility Criteria 2026

Before submitting your PC application for 2026 Karnataka, carefully verify that you meet all eligibility conditions. Candidates who do not meet the educational, age, or language criteria will be disqualified at any stage of the process.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must have passed Class 12 / PUC or an equivalent examination from a recognised board. This includes:

  • Class 12 passed from CBSE, ICSE, any State Board, or equivalent
  • Class 12 equivalent from NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling)
  • A 2-year ITC/Diploma (NVBT) course with one language and one academic subject from NIOS
  • A 3-year Diploma from a recognised Polytechnic institution (treated as equivalent to PUC for direct/compassionate recruitment)

Kannada Language Requirement: Candidates must have studied Kannada as a first or second language up to SSLC/10th standard. Those who have not done so must pass a Kannada Language Test conducted by KEA.

The KSP Constable apply online 2026 process is conducted through the KEA (Karnataka Examinations Authority) portal. Follow these steps carefully to submit a valid application for Karnataka police constable recruitment 2026.

  • Step 2: Click on the active link for KSP Civil Police Constable Recruitment 2026 (Adv. No. 01 or 02, depending on which cadre you are eligible for).
  • Step 3: Register by entering your personal, educational, and category details accurately.
  • Step 4: Choose the cadre (Kalyana-Karnataka or General) you are applying for. Note: only one application per notification is permitted.
  • Step 5: Upload a recent passport-size photograph (JPEG, 50KB-200KB) and your signature (JPEG, 50KB-70KB).
  • Step 6: Pay the required application fee online through the portal.
  • Step 7: Download and save a copy of the submitted application form and the fee payment receipt.

KSP Constable Selection Process 2026

The Karnataka police constable selection process 2026 consists of four clearly defined stages. Candidates must qualify each stage to proceed to the next. There is no direct interview; merit is determined through the written exam and physical assessments.

Shortlisted candidates (in a 1:2 ratio per vacancy) will undergo a comprehensive medical examination by a Medical Board. This includes vision testing, hearing assessment, and musculoskeletal evaluation to ensure candidates are physically fit for active police duty.

KSP Constable Salary 2026

One of the most attractive aspects of the KSP Recruitment 2026 is the government pay structure. Karnataka police constables are placed at Pay Level 7 under the 7th Pay Commission, with a monthly pay scale of Rs. 37,500 - Rs. 76,100. In addition to the base salary, candidates are eligible for:

  • Dearness Allowance (DA)
  • House Rent Allowance (HRA)
  • Travel Allowance (TA)
  • National Pension Scheme (NPS) benefits
  • Other Karnataka Government allowances

Training and Probation:

  • Selected candidates undergo 9 months of basic police training at designated Police Training Schools in Karnataka.
  • Candidates are on probation for 2 years and 6 months after formal appointment.
  • Candidates who fail during training may be removed from service.

The posts span three grade levels - MMGS II, MMGS III, and SMGS IV. Online applications open on 12 June 2026 and close on 28 June 2026. Experienced IT professionals in cloud engineering and AI/ML development should apply at the bank's official website, https://punjabandsind.bank.in/.

Punjab & Sind Bank has advertised 8 posts across five designations and two technology domains. All vacancies are contractual. The category-wise distribution is as follows.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

All eligibility conditions are assessed as on the respective cut-off dates stated above. Candidates must independently verify they meet every criterion before applying; merely submitting an application does not constitute a right to be called for selection.

Age Limit (as on 01 June 2026)

Scale Minimum Age Maximum Age Date of Birth Range
SMGS IV 33 years 45 years 02 June 1981 – 01 June 1993
MMGS III 31 years 43 years 02 June 1983 – 01 June 1995
MMGS II 29 years 41 years 02 June 1985 – 01 June 1997

The maximum ages above apply to General category and EWS candidates. SC/ST candidates receive 5 years of relaxation in the upper age limit; OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates receive 3 years; Persons with Benchmark Disabilities receive 10 years; Ex-Servicemen (with at least 5 years' military service) receive 5 years; and persons affected by the 1984 riots receive 5 years. SC/ST/OBC candidates may combine their category relaxation with only one of the remaining relaxation categories.

Educational Qualification and Work Experience

Post 1 - Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (MMGS II) Mandatory qualification: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Science & Engineering, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or Electronics & Communications Engineering (or equivalent) from a university/institute recognized by the Government of India, UGC, or AICTE. Preferred certifications include AWS Solutions Architect (Associate/Professional), Azure Administrator, DevOps Engineer, or Google Associate/Professional Cloud Engineer.

Work experience required: Minimum 4 years of post-qualification experience in IT Industry, BFSI, or the IT vertical of an organization, of which at least 2 years must be specifically in cloud administration or cloud engineering roles.

Post 2 - Manager, AI Engineers (MMGS II) Mandatory qualification: Full-time B.E./B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or Machine Learning - OR - full-time MCA/M.Tech in AI, Machine Learning, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field - from a university/institution recognized by the Government of India, AICTE, or UGC. Candidates must also hold at least one professional certification (valid as on the date of eligibility) in AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Data Science, or Generative AI from a recognized university, reputed technology organization, or professional certification body.

Work experience: Minimum 6 years (post B.E./B.Tech/MCA) in AI/ML development, Data Science, or Advanced Analytics, including at least 2 years leading or managing AI/ML projects or teams - OR - Minimum 5 years (post M.Tech) with the same specialization, including the same 2-year leadership requirement.

Post 3 - Senior Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (MMGS III) Same mandatory degree requirement as Post 1. Preferred certifications: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional), Azure Administrator, DevOps Engineer, or Google Associate/Professional Cloud Engineer.

Work experience: Minimum 6 years post-qualification experience in IT/BFSI, of which at least 3 years in cloud architecture or cloud engineering roles.

Post 4 - Senior Manager, AI Engineers (MMGS III) Same mandatory degree and certification requirements as Post 2 (Manager AI Engineers).

Work experience: Minimum 4 years (post B.E./B.Tech/MCA) in AI/ML development, Data Science, or Advanced Analytics - OR - Minimum 3 years (post M.Tech) in the same domains.

Post 5 - Chief Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (SMGS IV) Same mandatory degree as Posts 1 and 3, plus a mandatory intermediate certification from Microsoft Azure. Preferred additional qualifications: MCA or M.Tech/M.Sc in Computer Science, IT, or Electronics & Communications Engineering. Preferred certifications: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional), Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or Google Professional Cloud Architect.

Work experience: Minimum 8 years post-qualification experience in IT/BFSI, of which at least 4 years in cloud architecture, cloud engineering, or DevOps roles.

Candidates should note that 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%, and 54.99% as less than 55%, when calculating percentage of marks. Where a university awards CGPA/OGPA, candidates must convert it to percentage and indicate that figure in the online application.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is non-refundable. Payment must be made online only - cash, cheques, money orders, and postal stamps are not accepted. Bank transaction charges for the online payment gateway are borne by the candidate.

Category Application Fee
SC / ST / PwBD ₹100 + applicable taxes + payment gateway charges
General, EWS & OBC ₹850 + applicable taxes + payment gateway charges

Once submitted, an application cannot be withdrawn, and the fee will not be refunded under any circumstances, nor held in reserve for any other examination.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The bank will use a multi-stage selection process for all posts. All three scales - SMGS IV, MMGS III, and MMGS II - follow the same procedure: Written Test → Short-listing → Personal Interview.

The written test, where conducted, will have the following structure:

Section Questions Maximum Marks Duration
English Language 20 20 15 minutes
General Awareness 20 20 30 minutes
Professional Knowledge 60 60 60 minutes
Total 100 100 105 minutes

The minimum qualifying score in each section is 40% for General and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved Category candidates. However, only Professional Knowledge marks are used for drawing the merit/rank list and shortlisting candidates for the Personal Interview; marks in English Language and General Awareness are not included in the final merit calculation.

Candidates clearing the written test are called for a Personal Interview. The minimum qualifying score for the interview is 40% for Unreserved and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved categories. Final selection is based on the combined marks from the written test and Personal Interview, in order of merit ranking. Where two candidates tie at the cut-off, they are ranked in descending order of age.

The Personal Interview will be conducted in New Delhi unless otherwise specified. Call letters will be sent by email only. Candidates must attend at their own cost.

The bank shortlists candidates based on experience and suitability at its own discretion - meeting the minimum qualification does not guarantee an interview call.

Examination Centres

The bank has designated examination centres across India. Candidates may opt for a centre in their state, subject to availability. The bank reserves the right to allot a different centre or cancel/add centres. No request for a change of examination centre, date, or session will be entertained. Selected centres include: Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Guwahati (Assam), Patna and Bhagalpur (Bihar), Chandigarh/Mohali, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Delhi/Delhi-NCR, Panaji (Goa), Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar (Gujarat), Ambala (Haryana), Hamirpur (Himachal Pradesh), Jammu (J&K), Bengaluru (Karnataka), Ernakulam (Kerala), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Mumbai/Thane/Navi Mumbai/MMR (Maharashtra), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Patiala (Punjab), Jaipur (Rajasthan), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), Hyderabad (Telangana), Prayagraj, Lucknow and Meerut (Uttar Pradesh), Dehradun (Uttarakhand), and Asansol and Siliguri (West Bengal), among others.

Terms of Contract

This engagement is on a contractual basis, not a regular/permanent appointment. The initial period is three years, subject to annual performance review. Depending on need and performance, the bank may extend the contract on an annual basis for up to a maximum of two additional years at its discretion.

The bank may terminate the contract at any time without assigning any reason by giving one month's notice or paying one month's fixed component of compensation in lieu. Similarly, the appointee must give the bank one month's clear notice - or equivalent payment - to exit the contract before its expiry.

Additional conditions: the selected individual must not take up any assignment with any other organization during the contract period; no vigilance case or adverse observation from previous employers should be pending; and the candidate must have a minimum CIBIL score of 650 at the time of joining.

How to Apply

Applications are accepted online only through the bank's official website. The steps below reflect the application flow described in the notification.

  1. Visit https://punjabandsind.bank.in/ and navigate to the Recruitment section on the home page.
  2. Click on the relevant notification for Cloud CoE / AI Engineers.
  3. Before starting registration, scan and prepare the following files:
    • Passport-size photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm; 20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG/PNG)
    • Signature on white paper in black ink (10–20 KB)
    • Left thumb impression on white paper (20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG)
    • Hand-written declaration in English, on white paper in black ink - text: "I, [Name], hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." (50–100 KB; JPG/JPEG; NOT in capital letters)
    • Supporting documents in PDF format: Brief Resume, ID Proof, Age Proof, Educational Certificates, Experience Certificates/NOC, Caste Certificate (if applicable)
  4. Complete the online registration form. Keep the registered email ID and mobile number active throughout the process.
  5. Upload all documents at the specified fields. The system will not proceed until photographs and signatures meet specifications.
  6. Pay the application fee online. Transaction charges are borne by the candidate.
  7. Submit the application and save/print the system-generated application form with the registration number.
  8. Apply separately for each post if applying for more than one position.

In case of multiple submissions for the same post, only the last valid completed application will be retained; fees paid for earlier submissions will be forfeited.

Documents Required at Document Verification

Candidates called for the interview stage must bring originals and self-attested photocopies of all relevant documents. Documents not produced on the day of verification will disqualify the candidate from further participation.

Required documents include: Date of Birth proof (SSC/School Leaving Certificate); printout of call letter; system-generated online application printout; all educational certificates and mark sheets from Class X onwards (semester-wise mark sheets and provisional/final degree certificate); all work experience certificates and NOC from the current employer if employed with a public sector bank or government/quasi-government organization; caste/category certificates in the prescribed Government of India format (OBC certificate must be no more than one year old and contain the non-creamy layer clause); disability certificate from District Medical Board (if applicable); Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates, valid as on the date of application); two passport-size photographs identical to the one in the application; and valid photo identity proof (PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, Aadhaar, Employee ID, etc. - Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are not accepted).

No documents should be sent directly to the bank before or after the interview.

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes

Photo/Signature upload errors are among the most common reasons for application failure. Ensure your photograph is between 20 KB and 50 KB and your signature between 10 KB and 20 KB. Files larger than the specified limit will be rejected by the system. Use a scanner set to at least 200 DPI and save files in JPG/JPEG format. All supporting documents must be in PDF format.

Payment gateway failures can occur during high-traffic periods near the deadline. If a payment is deducted but the fee status is not updated, wait 24 hours and check again before attempting re-payment; duplicate payments are generally not refunded. Avoid applying on the last day to reduce the risk of server overload.

Hand-written declaration errors are a unique pitfall in this recruitment. The declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, in lowercase (not capital letters). A typed or third-party-written declaration will invalidate the application.

Name mismatches between the application and identity documents can cause disqualification at any stage. Ensure the name (and father's/husband's name where applicable) is spelled exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets. Candidates who have changed their name must produce an original Gazette notification, marriage certificate, or affidavit.

CIBIL score is a condition of joining, not selection. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying - a score below 650 will disqualify them at the time of joining even if selected.

The position of JRF does not confer any claim or right for regular appointment in URSC or in any ISRO/Department of Space centres.

ISRO URSC JRF Recruitment 2026  - Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for ISRO URSC JRF Recruitment 2026 is two-part: a qualifying postgraduate degree with the required minimum marks, and a valid national-level qualifying test score. Both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously as on the last date, i.e., 11 July 2026. Only passed candidates are eligible - students awaiting final results should not apply.

Educational Qualification

For positions JRF-E1 to JRF-E12, JRF-M1, JRF-M2, JRF-M3: M.E./M.Tech./M.Sc.(Engg.) or equivalent postgraduate degree in First Class with an aggregate minimum of 60% or CGPA/CPI of 6.5 on a 10-point scale.

For position JRF-E13 (M.Sc. route): M.Sc. in First Class with an aggregate minimum of 65% average of all semesters or CGPA/CPI of 6.84 on a 10-point scale.

For position JRF-E13 (M.Tech. route): M.Tech. or equivalent in First Class with an aggregate minimum of 60% or CGPA/CPI of 6.5 on a 10-point scale.

All degrees must be duly recognised by AICTE/UGC or any other organisation authorised by the Government of India. Essential qualifications must be completed within the stipulated duration of the course as prescribed by the university. Candidates who pursued professional courses through Open and Distance Learning (ODL) are not eligible to apply for JRF positions.

Where a university mentions both CGPA and percentage in its degree certificate or consolidated mark sheet, at least one criterion must meet DOS/ISRO eligibility norms. Conversion of CGPA into percentage of marks is not permitted to determine eligibility regardless of any conversion formula prescribed by the university. Rounding of percentage/CGPA is not allowed - values must be entered to the nearest 2 decimal places (e.g., 8.235 entered as 8.23; 8.236 as 8.24).

NET / NET-Equivalent Requirement

Candidates must have qualified one of the following national-level examinations. This is a mandatory requirement - possession of the degree alone does not make a candidate eligible to apply.

  • CSIR-UGC National Eligibility Test including NET-Lectureship (Assistant Professorship)
  • GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) conducted by MoE
  • JAM (Joint Admission Test) conducted by MoE
  • JEST (Joint Entrance Screening Test)
  • National level examinations conducted by Central Government Departments and their agencies/institutions such as DST, DBT, DAE, DOS, DRDO, MoE, ICAR, ICMR, IIT, IISc, IISER, NISER, etc.

Age Limit (as on 11 July 2026)

The maximum age for all JRF positions is 28 years as on 11 July 2026. Candidates wondering about age relaxation can note that SC/ST candidates get 5 years of relaxation and OBC candidates get 3 years. Additional relaxations as per Government of India orders apply to Ex-Servicemen, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, Widows, Divorced Women, and Women judicially separated from their husbands and not remarried.

Category Age Relaxation
SC / ST 5 years
OBC 3 years
Ex-Servicemen As per Government of India orders
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) As per Government of India orders
Widows, Divorced Women, Women judicially separated (not remarried) As per Government of India orders

ISRO URSC JRF Recruitment 2026  - Fellowship and Stipend

Selected JRFs at ISRO URSC receive a monthly fellowship stipend of ₹37,000 per month. After completion of two years as JRF, at the sole discretion of ISRO/DOS/URSC, the fellow may be awarded Senior Research Fellow (SRF) status with a stipend of ₹42,000 per month. HRA at prescribed rates is paid if hostel accommodation is not provided at the place of posting. Medical benefits for self are admissible as per extant rules. No Dearness Allowance (DA) is paid. The fellowship amount is treated as basic pay for this purpose.

JRFs are eligible only for casual leave. All female JRFs are entitled to maternity leave as per Government of India instructions. JRFs are also eligible for subsidised canteen facilities. Selected candidates are not entitled to any other benefits or concessions admissible to regular employees. The initial engagement is for two years, extendable based on assessment of work and project requirements. The maximum combined period of engagement as JRF and SRF together shall not exceed five years. JRFs with aptitude for research will be encouraged to register for a Ph.D. with an external university.

ISRO URSC JRF Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection for ISRO URSC JRF 2026 involves an initial screening stage followed by an interview. Meeting the minimum qualification is necessary but does not automatically entitle a candidate to be called for interview - shortlisting is based on academic performance and other parameters in the online application.

  1. Initial Screening - Based on academic performance and other parameters given in the online application. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for interview.
  2. Interview - Conducted in Bengaluru only on a given date. Call letters for the interview will be sent by e-mail only. The interview result will be announced on the ISRO website.

URSC/ISRO reserves the right to change the venue/date of the interview. Outstation candidates shortlisted for interview will be reimbursed to-and-fro Second Class Sleeper Railway fare by the shortest distance from the address in the online application to the interview venue, or non-A/C government bus fare, or actual fare - whichever is less - on production of proof of journey. If a candidate travels by a higher class, only second class rail fare excluding reservation/sleeper charges will be paid. Travel allowance is payable only to candidates allowed for interview after successful document verification.

How to Apply

Applications for ISRO URSC JRF Recruitment 2026 must be submitted online only. All further communications will be made exclusively by e-mail and through the ISRO website. Candidates are advised to check their e-mail regularly and visit www.isro.gov.in periodically for updates.

  1. Visit www.isro.gov.in and navigate to the "CAREERS" section
  2. Find Advertisement No. URSC:02:2026 and select the JRF position you wish to apply for
  3. Register online - note your Registration Number carefully and preserve it for future reference
  4. Fill in all required fields including a valid and correct e-mail ID - hall tickets will be sent by e-mail only
  5. Upload the following mandatory documents in soft copy:
    • Recent colour passport-size photograph (not older than 6 months) - JPG/JPEG, maximum 500 KB
    • Signature - JPG/JPEG, maximum 500 KB
    • Mark cards of each semester/year with final pass certificate - single PDF, not exceeding 1 MB
    • SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/Ex-Serviceman certificate if seeking age relaxation - PDF, not exceeding 1 MB
    • CSIR-UGC-NET score card or GATE score card or equivalent national examination score card - PDF, not exceeding 1 MB
  6. Submit the application before 11 July 2026
  7. Candidates already employed under Central/State Government, Public Sector Undertaking, or Autonomous Body must follow up the online application with a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer, indicating name, position applied for, Position No., and Registration No. on the reverse of the NOC
  8. Avoid submitting multiple applications for the same position - if multiple applications are submitted, only the latest application submitted before the closing date will be processed

For any clarification, candidates may write to [email protected]. No interim correspondence will otherwise be entertained. Canvassing in any form will result in disqualification of candidature.

Document Requirements at Interview

Shortlisted candidates called for the interview must bring originals and self-attested photocopies of all of the following documents to the interview venue in Bengaluru.

  • All certificates and mark sheets of all degrees and postgraduate degree
  • Equivalency Certificate from Association of Indian Universities, New Delhi - in case of a foreign degree
  • Proof of work experience
  • Age proof
  • CSIR-UGC-NET score card or GATE score card or score card of equivalent national level examination
  • Caste certificate - for SC/ST/OBC candidates seeking age relaxation
  • PwBD certificate - for candidates claiming PwBD age relaxation
  • Relevant certificates issued by Competent Authority for Ex-Servicemen and other categories claiming age relaxation

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes

Applying through an online government portal involves several steps where errors can cause rejection. The following general guidance helps candidates complete their application successfully.

  • Photo upload errors: The photograph must be in JPG/JPEG format, not older than 6 months, and not exceeding 500 KB. Uploading any object other than your own passport-size photograph in the designated photo field will result in your candidature being rejected at screening stage under any circumstances.
  • Incomplete applications rejected outright: Applications submitted without complete information or without a photograph will be summarily rejected. Verify every mandatory field before final submission.
  • Last-day server load: Online portals experience high traffic close to the deadline. Submit your application well before 11 July 2026 to avoid gateway timeouts or submission failures.
  • Save your Registration Number: Upon successful registration, an online Registration Number is provided. Store it securely - it is required for all future reference, hall ticket download, and communications.
  • E-mail ID accuracy: The e-mail ID entered in the application must be valid and actively monitored. Hall tickets and all official communications will be sent exclusively by e-mail. Errors in e-mail ID cannot be corrected after submission.
  • Multiple applications: If you accidentally submit more than one application for the same position, only the latest application submitted before the closing date will be processed. Ensure that application is complete in all respects.
  • PDF file size: Each supporting document PDF must not exceed 1 MB. Compress your PDF if the file is larger before uploading.
  • ODL degree: Candidates who completed their qualifying postgraduate degree through Open and Distance Learning are not eligible. Verify your mode of study before applying.

Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), a Scientific Society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, has announced its JIT (Just-In-Time) June 2026 Recruitment Cycle with 900+ contractual vacancies across 11 centres including Bengaluru, Chennai, Noida, Pune, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Delhi, Mohali, Kolkata, Thiruvananthapuram, and Guwahati (CINE/North East). Applications are open from 01 June 2026 and the last date to apply online is 20 June 2026. There is no application fee for any category. All applications must be submitted online at https://careers.cdac.in/.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Quick Overview

C-DAC has published separate notifications dated 01 June 2026 for each of its 11 centres. Each centre-specific advertisement covers post details, domain areas, qualification, experience, age limit, and selection instructions. The number of positions is provisional and may vary based on actual project requirements.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Important Dates

Candidates planning to apply for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment should note these key dates. All eligibility conditions — age, qualification, and experience — are calculated as on the last date of application, i.e., 20 June 2026.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Centre-wise Vacancy Details

C-DAC JIT June 2026 vacancies are spread across 11 centres pan-India, covering domains ranging from AI/ML and Cyber Security to VLSI, HPC, Quantum Computing, Embedded Systems, and e-Governance. Each centre has issued its own advertisement — applying on one centre's portal does not cover other centres.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Post-wise Eligibility and Salary

C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment covers positions from entry-level Project Associates to senior Project Managers. C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

C-DAC charges no application fee for any position under the JIT June 2026 Recruitment Cycle. This applies to all candidates across all categories — General, EWS, OBC, SC, ST, and PwBD — and across all 11 centres. No payment of any kind is required at any stage of the application process.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

C-DAC follows a multi-stage selection process for JIT June 2026 positions. All communications regarding selection stages are sent by email only — no hard copy letters or call letters are dispatched at any stage.

Stage 1 – Initial Academic Screening: All submitted applications are assessed on the basis of academic records, qualifications, declared experience, and domain relevance. Only candidates meeting minimum eligibility criteria proceed further. C-DAC reserves the right to raise the minimum cut-off if the applicant volume significantly exceeds the number of vacancies.

Stage 2 – Written Test (if applicable): A written or skill-based test may be conducted at the discretion of individual centres, depending on the number of screened-in candidates. Shortlisted candidates will be notified by email. No TA/DA is paid for attending the written test.

Stage 3 – Personal Interview: Candidates who clear the screening and written test stages are called for a personal interview by the respective C-DAC centre. The interview call is sent by email only. Receipt of an interview call letter does not confirm selection. No TA/DA is paid for attending the interview.

Important Points About the Nature of Engagement

These C-DAC positions are purely contractual — candidates should understand the terms before applying. The initial contract period is up to 3 years (1 year for the Kolkata centre), or project completion, whichever is earlier. Extensions are possible based on performance and project requirements.

Selected candidates have no right to regular or permanent appointment in C-DAC by virtue of this engagement. They may be deputed or transferred to any C-DAC project location across India based on organizational requirement. C-DAC internal candidates who are finally selected must resign from their current C-DAC service and join afresh for the selected post. Internal C-DAC candidates must also have completed a minimum of 2 years of service in C-DAC as on 20 June 2026 to be eligible.

Competition Level Analysis

C-DAC JIT June 2026 is a large-scale national recruitment drive and competition is expected to be moderate to high, particularly in popular domains. The absence of any application fee significantly increases applicant volume across all centres.

Roles in AI/ML, Full Stack Development, Cyber Security, and Software Development at the Project Engineer and Senior Project Engineer levels will attract the largest applicant pools, especially from tier-2 and tier-3 engineering colleges. In contrast, niche domain posts in Quantum Computing, VLSI/Chip Design, Additive Manufacturing, Robotics, and HPC System Software will see comparatively lower competition but demand highly specialised credentials.

Initial screening is where effective filtering happens — CGPA, subject percentage, and domain match are the primary screening parameters. Candidates applying to Noida (e-Governance, Health Informatics) and Pune (200+ positions, wide domain breadth) should expect steeper competition due to location preference and higher vacancy counts. Documenting relevant project work, publications, or domain-specific internships may help distinguish profiles at the screening stage, even where such work is not formally counted as experience.

Who Should NOT Apply

Before investing time in the application, certain candidates should assess whether this recruitment is suitable for them.

Candidates seeking a permanent government job should not apply — all positions are purely contractual with no path to regular employment in C-DAC. Those whose degree is from an institution not approved by AICTE/UGC or not recognized by the Central or State Government will face rejection during document verification. Candidates unable to produce a CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate from their university — where applicable — will also face issues at document stage.

Work experience from internships, academic project placements, teaching assignments, or research work embedded in a curriculum is explicitly excluded from the experience count unless a specific post states otherwise. Candidates without formal employer-issued experience certificates clearly showing period of employment, designation, and salary drawn will find their experience claims unacceptable. C-DAC internal candidates who have not completed 2 years of service by 20 June 2026 are ineligible. Anyone unwilling to be posted anywhere in India, or who prefers postal communication over email-only correspondence, will find this recruitment unsuitable.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Several avoidable errors frequently affect candidates during the C-DAC application process. Applying on one centre's portal and assuming it covers other centres is the most common mistake — each centre has a completely separate advertisement and application link, and candidates must apply individually to each centre they wish to be considered for. Similarly, candidates who want to be considered for more than one position must submit a separate application for each post.

Uploading a resume in any format other than PDF (max 500 KB) or a photograph other than .jpg (max 400 KB) will cause application issues. Failing to note the unique application number generated after submission is another frequent problem — this number is essential for all future reference. Government or PSU employees who do not forward their application through proper channel must ensure they carry a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their current employer at the time of the interview. Sending physical documents or hard copies to any C-DAC centre is unnecessary — the entire application process is online. Assuming an interview call letter means confirmed selection is also incorrect; candidature remains provisional until document verification is completed.

How to Apply

Candidates must apply online only through the official C-DAC careers portal. A valid mobile number and active email ID are mandatory, as OTP-based login is used and all subsequent communications are sent by email.

  1. Visit the official C-DAC careers portal at https://careers.cdac.in/.
  2. Select the relevant centre from the list of active advertisements.
  3. Click 'Apply' against the specific position you wish to apply for.
  4. Log in using your registered mobile number and enter the OTP received.
  5. Fill in all required fields in the online application form accurately.
  6. Upload your passport-size photograph in .jpg format (max 400 KB) and your resume/CV in PDF format (max 500 KB).
  7. Submit the form and note down the unique application number generated upon successful submission.
  8. If applying for multiple positions or multiple centres, repeat the process with a separate application for each.

Documents to be produced at the time of document verification or joining include: educational mark sheets and degree certificates from Class 10 onwards, CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate (if applicable), experience certificates from all previous and current employers, caste/category certificate (if applicable), disability certificate issued by the District Medical Board (for PwBD candidates), date of birth proof, and an NOC from the current employer where applicable.

Eligibility Criteria for FSSAI Deputation Posts 2026
